70a136f4ec833922: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — It’s been three days since the last show of The Weeknd’s After Hours Til Dawn Tour (AHTD) in Kuala Lumpur which also marked the end of his epic world tour.

Videos and photos from his final two shows at the TM National Stadium in Bukit Jalil continue to make the rounds on social media, while his songs continue to be heard on local radio stations such as HITZ, Fly FM and ERA FM.
Some fans travelled thousands of miles to be part of the experience, while others just had to take a train or car ride from their homes to the two shows here.
One artist, seven shows, three countries and two continents
Layla Hackner, 22, from Austria was among the 130,000 fans in KL who sang and danced their hearts out to The Weeknd, whose real name is Abel Tesfaye.
She went to all three of his Munich shows in Germany last June as well as both nights of The Weeknd’s Ireland stop in Dublin in August. The two-night finale in KL marked her seventh AHTD show.
“After travelling all the way from Austria, I couldn’t have asked for a better ending. Kuala Lumpur definitely made it worth it!,” she said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Layla Hackner (far left) attended seven shows on The Weeknd’s ‘After Hours Til Dawn Tour’, including both nights of the Kuala Lumpur finale. — Picture courtesy of Layla Hackner

Hackner said she initially planned to go to just that one show in Munich but somewhere along the way, she was motivated to experience more of the tour which became the perfect opportunity for her to explore the world.
“I honestly never planned for any of this to happen. Most of the additional trips were quite impulsive decisions.”

Despite that, going to seven shows across two continents does come with its own set of challenges and the biggest one for Hackner was securing the presale tickets for the Asia leg where she had to wake up around 3am (Central European time) to secure her tickets back in May.
“I think one of the things I appreciate most about Abel as an artist is that he’s a storyteller. You can see that in his music, but you can also feel it throughout his live performances.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Layla Hackner and her friend at The Weeknd’s ‘After Hours Til Dawn Tour’ concert at TM National Stadium in Bukit Jalil. — Picture courtesy of Layla Hackner
A new benchmark for concerts in Malaysia?
For 28-year-old Juhan Shameerul Shaharuzaman, years of listening to The Weeknd finally culminated in a fan moment where he got to touch the singer’s hand.
“I was at the end of the barricade and it was like a full hand touch (from The Weeknd).
“It felt like a blessing. I kissed my hand at least three times after that,” Juhan told Malay Mail.
He first discovered the singer’s music through his brother in 2015, Juhan gradually developed an appreciation for his discography, eventually introducing his songs to friends and university mates.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Shameerul Shaharuzaman (back row, centre) and Muzafar Rais Marwazi (far left) at the first night of The Weeknd’s ‘After Hours Til Dawn Tour’ finale in Kuala Lumpur. — Picture courtesy of Muzafar Rais Marwazi
Meanwhile, marketing executive Muzafar Rais Marwazi is still wrapping his head around the fact that The Weeknd has chosen KL as his closing AHTD tour stop.

“It’s crazy how he chose to end his era or his tour of four years in our country. I mean, what made us so special? He could’ve ended it in Thailand or Indonesia but no, he chose us,” said the 34-year-old.
For these three fans, the show(s) may be over but the music definitely plays on.
cca9be9b39b6bd97: DOHA: Malaysia is considering accelerating its quantum migration process to strengthen national data security amid advances in quantum computing technology that are expected to pose new challenges to cybersecurity systems.

Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said he had asked the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission to hold discussions with the National Security Council, the National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) and telecommunications companies to explore potential collaboration in this area.
He said the collaboration would involve establishing a research and development space to facilitate faster and more secure quantum migration in Malaysia.
He said this when commenting on technological innovations that could benefit Malaysia after visiting several exhibition booths at the Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026 here yesterday.
Fahmi said one of the technological innovations that caught his attention was quantum-safe communication, which is becoming increasingly important for future data protection.
He said the emergence of quantum computers on the market was expected to pose significant challenges to existing cryptography and encryption methods used to safeguard data.
"I foresee that quantum migration and quantum-safe communication will be among the key issues facing many countries in the years ahead.
"Quantum computers are expected to enter the market in the near future, posing major challenges to existing cryptography and encryption methods used to ensure our data remains secure," he said.

Apart from quantum technology, Fahmi said his visit to the exhibition booths also provided an opportunity to explore various innovations, including the integration of artificial intelligence into smart city services and security systems.

Quantum migration refers to the process of upgrading existing digital security systems to adopt quantum-resistant encryption technologies designed to protect data against potential threats from future quantum computers.
6ac505116bf1aeb9: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Traffic flow on most major expressways nationwide remained smooth as of 8am today, but vehicle numbers are expected to increase later in the day as motorists return from the Deepavali and additional school holidays.

However, a Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) spokesperson said congestion was reported along the southbound stretch of the North-South Expressway (PLUS), from Yong Peng towards Ayer Hitam, following an accident.
“The accident, which occurred at Kilometre 82.3, involved a lorry and a car, but no fatalities were reported,” he told Bernama when contacted this morning.
The spokesperson said CCTV monitoring had yet to show a significant increase in traffic heading towards the Klang Valley, possibly due to the additional holiday today.
“Traffic volume is expected to increase between 10 am and 11 am as motorists return to the federal capital from the north, south and East Coast,” he added.
In view of the ongoing Northeast Monsoon, LLM advised highway users to maintain a safe following distance to reduce the risk of incidents involving sudden braking.

“Motorists are also advised to stop and rest at rest and service areas (R&Rs) if they feel tired or sleepy, while motorcyclists are encouraged to use the shelters provided by LLM and highway concessionaires during rainy conditions,” the spokesperson said.
For the latest traffic updates, the public can call LLM’s toll-free hotline at 1800-88-7752. — Bernama
730cd716c5f635d4: KUALA LUMPUR: Selangor coach Kim Pan Gon refused to discuss his side's 2-0 defeat to Kuching City in the second leg of the FA Cup semi-final, instead calling for a Malaysian Football League (MFL) investigation into an incident involving midfielder Nazmi Faiz Mansor.
Kuching booked their place in the final with a 3-2 aggregate victory at the Taha Ariffin Stadium in Kuching on Sunday, sealed by a 119th-minute own goal from Mukhairi Ajmal Mahadi.

However, the late goal was followed by a heated confrontation near the touchline involving members of both teams' dugouts, with referee Izwan Abdullah showing red cards to Selangor playmaker Eduardo Sosa and fitness coach Joel Josep Dones Charte.
Pan Gon was visibly upset during his post-match press conference, choosing to focus on Nazmi's approach towards Selangor's technical area rather than the result.
"You saw that. A player scoring a goal cannot come over to the opposite bench to attack the head coach," he said.
"That was number eight, Nazmi. That made everybody get involved."
Asked what he meant by "attack", Pan Gon said Nazmi had moved aggressively towards him.
"He came to attack. He came close and behaved disgracefully in front of me. Our players and staff thought he might touch me, so they wanted to stand in front of me to protect me."
The former Harimau Malaya coach also defended his players and staff, who were shown red cards during the confrontation.

"I don't think our staff and players deserved red cards. What would you expect them to do if an opponent came close to the head coach? They wanted to protect me. If they hadn't stepped in, I don't know what would have happened," he said.
The South Korean insisted the incident warranted an investigation, regardless of the result.
"Games can be won or lost. That doesn't matter. But there must be fair play, sportsmanship and respect for the opponent," said Pan Gon.
"Don't come to the opposite bench to attack the head coach. That's very disappointing. MFL has to investigate."
Kuching coach Aidil Sharin Sahak offered a different take when asked about the dramatic match.
"Well, maybe we watched Korean drama today," he said, before suggesting Pan Gon should examine his own team's disciplinary record and conduct during the match.

8cbd44a03b3084eb: KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood victims in Perak recorded a slight increase while the situation in Selangor continued to show a downward trend, with a total of 654 people still sheltering at temporary relief centres (PPS) as of this morning.
The situation in Hilir Perak saw the number of victims increase to 439 people from 130 families this morning, compared with 414 people from 123 families yesterday evening.

The state Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said 277 victims from 84 families were housed at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council (MPTI) Rest House Hall PPS, while another 136 people from 39 families were taking shelter at the MPTI Langkap Hall.

Meanwhile, 26 victims from seven families remained at the Manjung Community Hall PPS, comprising residents of Pekan Beruas, Taman Beruas, Taman Desa, Perumahan Awam, Taman Seri Delima, Taman Limau Emas, Taman Anggerik, Kampung Kilang, Kampung Dendang and Kampung Paya Lima.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecast rain and thunderstorms in all districts in Perak this afternoon and tonight.
In addition, water levels in two rivers were reported to have exceeded the danger level, namely Sungai Kinta in Tanjung Tualang at 13.78m and Sungai Bidor in Changkat Jong at 3.53m.
In Selangor, the situation improved, with the number of victims at PPS decreasing to 215 people from 55 families as of 8am today, compared with 507 people from 143 families yesterday.

According to the Welfare Department's InfoBencana portal, two PPS were operating in Kuala Selangor, namely SK Parit Mahang, which housed 100 people from 23 families, and SK Jaya Setia (68 victims, 20 families), while SK Dato' Maharaja Lela remained activated despite having no occupants recorded.
In Shah Alam, 47 victims from 11 families were reported to be taking shelter at the Dewan Siantan Kampung Melayu Subang, Section U6 PPS.

Meanwhile, the Drainage and Irrigation Department's National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre, in a statement last night, said nine districts in Kelantan were expected to be affected by floods, namely Kota Baru, Tumpat, Bachok, Machang, Pasir Mas, Pasir Puteh, Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai and Jeli.

The centre also forecast that several areas in Pahang, namely Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin, could be affected by floods from yesterday until Wednesday, particularly in high-risk locations and low-lying areas.
In Terengganu, a similar alert was issued for six districts, namely Setiu, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus, Besut, Hulu Terengganu and Marang.
54f1f9ea2dd70e43: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — As campaigning for the 16th Melaka state election enters its second week, rival parties are seeking to win over voters with promises of economic growth, political stability and reform, while new alliances face the test of whether their supporters will vote across party lines.

Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) are banking on their joint electoral machinery, Pakatan Harapan (PH) is challenging the incumbent administration’s record, and smaller parties are seeking to distinguish themselves through reform pledges and alternative campaign strategies.
A total of 79 candidates are contesting 28 state seats in the November 14 election, with early voting scheduled for November 10.

PH is contesting 24 seats, followed by BN with 23, Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) with 16, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) with seven, PN with five and Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia (Putra) with one. Three candidates are running as independents.
Here is how the main parties are making their case, the issues shaping the campaign and the key contests to watch as polling day approaches.
BN-PN: Promising continuity and growth

BN and PN are presenting a united front through their Muafakat Melaka arrangement, with caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh leading their campaign pitch on development and economic growth.

Their joint manifesto promises to attract RM30 billion in investments, provide free domestic water for households consuming less than 20 cubic metres a month and freeze quit rent increases for five years.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional are campaigning under the Muafakat Melaka arrangement, promising economic growth and development while seeking to consolidate support among their respective voters. — Bernama pic

Other proposals include establishing Melaka as a national technical and vocational education and training (TVET) hub, providing financial assistance to B40 students pursuing TVET qualifications and offering funding to small traders.
Ab Rauf has also defended his administration’s record, claiming BN has fulfilled 97 per cent of the promises made in its 2021 state election manifesto.
However, PH chairman Adly Zahari has challenged that figure, arguing that BN should account for its earlier commitments before making fresh ones.
BN’s campaign is also seeking to demonstrate unity between Umno and PAS, with their cooperation presented as a continuation of their electoral partnership in Negeri Sembilan.

BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has urged both parties’ campaign machinery to respect one another and avoid clashes, underscoring the challenge of managing their previous political differences.
Beyond policy announcements, BN has brought familiar faces into its campaign.
After previously enlisting Chinese actress Fan Bingbing to promote Melaka internationally, Ab Rauf brought veteran Malaysian actor Datuk Jalaluddin Hasan to campaign in the Bukit Katil constituency.

At the constituency level, Duyong incumbent Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem, who has built a following on social media, said he was not offering a specific manifesto this time, arguing that addressing residents’ problems was already his responsibility as their elected representative.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Pakatan Harapan is seeking to challenge BN’s record in Melaka, focusing on governance, economic opportunities and unfulfilled promises while navigating its partnership with the coalition at the federal level. — Bernama pic
PH: Challenging BN’s record
For PH, the challenge is to convince voters that it offers a credible alternative to BN, despite both coalitions being part of the federal unity government.

Its manifesto, Aspirasi Melaka Rumah Kita, is built around three main pillars and 12 priorities, including transparent administration, the Smart Melaka transformation, economic opportunities for young people and stronger tourism development.
The coalition is also targeting younger voters with a proposal to allocate 30 per cent of local authority work contracts to young people, alongside pledges on employment, housing and public welfare.
Prime Minister and PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has highlighted the coalition’s multiracial appeal and the integrity of its candidates as key strengths.
PH is making BN’s record in state government a central campaign issue, with Adly repeatedly questioning its delivery of previous manifesto commitments and the lower jobs target in its latest pledges.

The coalition has also been holding daily 10am press conferences at its main operations room in Bukit Baru, featuring Adly, acting Melaka PKR state leadership council chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim and Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong.
The regular briefings allow PH to respond to campaign developments, challenge BN-PN and keep its policy positions in the public eye.

Some PH leaders have also urged voters to assess the coalition based on the federal government’s record, with Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Karim arguing that its national performance should be part of voters’ considerations.
However, PH must distinguish its state-level agenda from BN’s while remaining its partner in Putrajaya, a balancing act that complicates its campaign against the incumbent administration.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Bersatu is contesting seven seats under its own banner, positioning itself as an alternative to BN amid political differences with PAS and the wider Perikatan Nasional alliance. — Picture via Facebook/ts.muhyiddin
Bersatu: Taking on BN amid PAS tensions
Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia is seeking to position itself as an alternative to BN while navigating tensions with PAS that have complicated the PN campaign.
The party is contesting seven seats under its own logo, separately from PN’s five candidates.

Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said some voters remained confused about the distinction between Bersatu and PN, prompting him to instruct party leaders to clarify its position during the campaign.

At a mega ceramah in Pantai Kundor, Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali accused PAS and Wawasan of betraying the mandate previously given to PN voters by cooperating with parties they had once campaigned against.
He also pointed to political turmoil in Negeri Sembilan, arguing that BN and Umno had failed to provide stable government despite their electoral success there.
Azmin urged Melaka voters not to give BN another opportunity to govern, warning that the state could face similar instability.

Muhyiddin, meanwhile, has returned to a familiar campaign argument by highlighting his record as prime minister during the Covid-19 pandemic, recalling his administration’s handling of the country during the lockdowns.
The approach echoes his previous state election and by-election campaigns since the 15th general election, when his pandemic-era leadership featured prominently in his appeal to voters.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Parti Bersama Malaysia has combined grassroots campaigning with livestreamed ceramah and reform pledges, seeking to reach voters beyond traditional campaign events. — Picture via Facebook/rafiziramli.bersama
Bersama: Reform pledges and digital campaigning

Among the smaller parties, Bersama is combining conventional ceramah and grassroots engagement with an extensive online presence, adopting an approach similar to its previous Johor election campaigns.
The party was the first to launch its manifesto for the Melaka election and has placed reform at the centre of its campaign.
Its Jelajah Trak Kancil campaign involves candidates and party leaders holding ceramah from a small truck, usually beginning around 9pm, with the events streamed live on YouTube.
Based on observations of the livestreams, the broadcasts have drawn about 80,000 views each, extending the party’s reach beyond those attending in person.
Former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli and his media team have also been accompanying candidates on the ground.
Bersama has revived familiar reform messages from previous elections, including inviting Teoh Lee Lan, the sister of the late Teoh Beng Hock, to one of its campaign events.

All 16 Bersama candidates signed a pledge calling for a fresh investigation into Teoh’s death, the introduction of an Anti-Torture Act and comprehensive reforms of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission.
The party is also using government data to scrutinise the incumbent administration, with Rafizi highlighting what he described as an increasingly unsustainable state financial position.
Bersama has used the figures to call for better revenue collection and a review of spending priorities, reflecting Rafizi’s data-driven approach to scrutinising public administration.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Jobs, the cost of living and the impact of development projects on local communities are among the key concerns shaping voter sentiment ahead of the November 14 polls, according to a political analyst. — Bernama pic
Voter sentiment: Jobs, living costs and stability

Despite the competing political narratives, campaigning has been relatively subdued, with local economic concerns taking precedence over national political rhetoric, according to political analyst Amir Fareed Rahim.

The strategic director of consultancy KRA Group said jobs and the cost of living remained key concerns, but voters were also questioning whether development projects were delivering tangible benefits to local communities.

“From our observation, key issues raised by these voters centre around whether tourism is improving local livelihoods, what coastal reclamation means for fishing communities, and how the state will deal with worsening traffic,” he told Malay Mail.
Political stability is another consideration, given that Melaka has had several chief ministers since 2018.
Amir Fareed said criticism of delayed projects could work both ways for BN, raising questions about its delivery while also reminding voters of the importance of continuity.
He said BN had an advantage among voters who credited Ab Rauf with development and welfare initiatives, while PH retained support in areas where its candidates had addressed local grievances.
Non-Malay voters, however, faced a more complicated choice, with some disappointed by the pace of federal reforms while remaining uneasy about Umno’s cooperation with PAS.
That unease could help PH retain support, although disappointment with the federal government’s reform agenda could also affect turnout, he said.

Amir Fareed said BN-PN had the clearest path to forming the state government, citing BN’s incumbency, Ab Rauf’s development record and more coordinated cooperation between Umno and PAS than in the previous two state elections.
The real test, however, would be whether that cooperation translated into votes in constituencies where the parties were supporting one another’s candidates.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Pakatan Harapan candidate for Paya Rumput, Datuk Azman Abidin, watches former national footballers, including Safee Sali and Mat Yo, in action during a football clinic held as part of his Melaka election campaign. Paya Rumput is among the key battlegrounds where voter turnout and shifting political loyalties could influence the outcome of the November 14 polls. — Bernama pic
Key battlegrounds: Where votes could swing
Among the seats to watch is Paya Rumput, where BN won by just 629 votes in 2021.
PAS is contesting the seat under the BN-PN arrangement, while PKR has fielded Anwar’s political secretary, Azman Abidin.

Amir Fareed said his team’s observations showed Umno and PAS campaigning closely together there, but the question remained whether BN supporters would turn out for a PAS candidate and whether Azman’s profile could help PKR attract Malay voters.
Bemban is another constituency to watch, with PN fielding a Wawasan candidate while Bersatu is contesting separately.
Amir Fareed said his team observed a strong Wawasan presence during the candidate’s walkabout, adding that the result could indicate how much support PN had retained since the 2022 general election.
For PH, the immediate tests include whether Amanah can retain Bukit Katil and DAP can defend Ayer Keroh, while PKR will be seeking to regain Machap Jaya and Kelebang.

In mixed constituencies such as DAP-held Ayer Keroh, where Malay voters make up roughly 42 per cent of the electorate, even relatively small shifts in support or turnout could influence the outcome, he said.
Amir Fareed said PH had room to make gains in a campaign that was less confrontational than the Johor state election, with Budget 2027 potentially giving it a boost.
However, Bersama, which has Rafizi playing a prominent campaign role, had been organising in Melaka even before the state assembly was dissolved and could draw support from the same pool of voters.

He also identified the controversy surrounding former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest bid as a possible factor affecting PH supporters’ motivation to vote during the second week of campaigning.

Ultimately, Amir Fareed said the election would test whether voters were willing to transfer their support across newly formed political alliances, particularly when their preferred party was not contesting under its own banner.
25f6e64abf7523d0: WASHINGTON, Nov 9 — Donald Trump vowed a political comeback yesterday as the major parties clashed over Democrat threats to prosecute top administration officials after the president’s Republicans lost control of Congress in midterm elections.

The devastating results in last Tuesday’s vote leave Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year ‘lame duck’ period of his White House tenure. It also opens the door to multiple investigations by the Democrat-controlled Congress of the president, his family and senior members of his administration.

On political talk shows Sunday, incoming congressional leaders from the Democratic Party promised to hold Trump and his aides to account, while the president’s top law officer resolved to defend them and Trump dug in his heels on social media.

“America took a giant step back in History with the results of the last Election,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social, adding that the stock market that had grown during his tenure took a loss after the vote.
“But have no fear, we will be back, BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!”

On Friday, a defiant Trump appointed hardline advisor Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback — even though many Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, have reflected on why they had lost so badly at the ballot box.
Miller was architect of Trump’s tough immigration policy, which analysts have identified as a contributing factor to the unpopularity of Republicans and their election debacle.

Amid Democrat threats for administration officials to “lawyer up,” Trump said Saturday he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration, likening it to “extortion.”
Impeaching Hegseth?
With control of committees in both chambers of Congress, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny.

Likely subjects include the Trump family’s business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war.

Hakeem Jeffries, set to become speaker of the new Democrat-controlled House of Representatives, said he would support an effort to oust Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, a key architect of the war on Iran that began in February.
“I’m a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution,” Jeffries told ABC, when asked about a Republican lawmaker’s reported plan to introduce an impeachment motion as early as Monday.

“The so-called secretary of defense has abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe. Pete Hegseth has got to go.”

Trump on Sunday defended Hegseth when talking with reporters, saying: “I mean he’s guilty of two things, basically winning two wars,” referring to the US raid on Venezuela in January that removed president Nicholas Maduro and the ongoing war with Iran.
“We won in Venezuela. We’ve taken out hundreds of billions of dollars. We won in 48 minutes. And we won in Iran,” Trump told reporters. “It’s just a question of closing it out now or later.”
Attorney General Todd Blanche, a former personal lawyer for Trump and now head of the Justice Department, vowed to actively defend Trump and senior members of his administration.
“If they try to come after Stephen Miller…instead of actually just conducting oversight and leading, of course the Department of Justice will be there to defend him,” Blanche told CNN.
Robert Garcia, the ranking Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, took aim at Blanche, saying one role of Congress under the US constitution is to hold the executive branch to account.

“All he wants to do is protect Donald Trump, is protect Donald Trump’s cabinet and administration officials. That is not his job,” Garcia told CNN, vowing to stop corruption and investigate “those that are committing crimes against the American public.”
“They can come after us however they want. We’re not going to be intimidated,” added Garcia. — AFP

cfdd249f68becd71: AYER KEROH: Malaysia must reduce its dependence on foreign labour in phases by expanding the adoption of automation, robotics and digital technology, particularly within the manufacturing sector.

Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said this approach is crucial to ensure the sustainability of domestic industry without remaining perpetually reliant on foreign workers to meet operational needs.
"Our country already has 2.6 million foreign workers, and under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), we must control this figure gradually.

"We cannot rely on foreign workers for everything. We need to identify mechanisms that allow businesses in Malaysia to operate without being completely dependent on foreign labour," he told reporters after attending a dialogue session with the business community in Melaka yesterday.
Johari said foreign labour is still required for roles categorised as 3D — dirty, difficult and dangerous — but industry must transition towards a more sustainable business model.

He said prolonged reliance on foreign labour is not a viable long-term solution, as experienced personnel must eventually return to their home countries, compelling employers to train new recruits from scratch.
He added that the manufacturing sector in particular needs to ramp up the adoption of technology, including artificial intelligence, robotics and automation, to create higher-skilled jobs.
Such a shift, he said, is also vital to provide more suitable career opportunities for educated and skilled local talent.
"I understand this is not easy, as our culture of dependency on foreign labour has been deeply entrenched for a very long time.
"Therefore, this transition is not something that can be achieved in a year or two. It requires time," he said.

Meanwhile, Johari said the local workforce, including Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) graduates, must be granted more opportunities to gain practical experience and master industry skills.

He added that there was a need to explore ways to retain the expertise of experienced foreign workers in manufacturing, whilst simultaneously intensifying training for local staff to enable them to take over those roles.
55b73e551f7bb44a: SAO PAULO: Lewis Hamilton made a subdued exit from Interlagos on Sunday after a weekend to forget at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, the third race in a disappointing 'triple-header' for Ferrari.

The seven-time champion finished ninth after starting 20th on the grid, two places behind teammate Charles Leclerc, after a rain-hit contest where Ferrari were amongst the also-rans as Mercedes clinched the constructors' title.
Ferrari remained second in the teams' standings but needing only three more points that their rival Mercedes cruised to the world title with little concern on the day.
The result saw Hamilton slip from third to fourth in the drivers' title race behind new champion Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes, Max Verstappen of Red Bull and Mercedes' George Russell. Leclerc is fifth.

Hamilton, ahead of his 400th Formula One race start, had started the weekend declaring that he and Leclerc had squashed the unrest and tension that lay between them in the team after a first lap tangle in Mexico, but his raised optimism did not produce results.
"It was a really tough day and weekend for the whole team," he said.
"They have done a really great job - especially all the mechanics in switching the engines and making sure the car was as good as it could be."
Hamilton had engine problems on Friday and had to introduce two new units on Saturday as another one failed during final practice. It led to him being penalised and starting 20th.
"I had a great start in the race, but unfortunately the rear tyre just ballooned and over-heated and after that on slicks I was feeling pretty good.
"It was very tricky in these conditions, and we ended up making an extra stop so I had a lot of ground to cover."
He said he spun late in the race because he did not realise how wet it had become.

"I didn't hear that it was raining more in the first sector and I passed the pit lane, got to turn one and it was wet. So that unfortunately, lost us a couple of places, but otherwise the team did a great job." - AFP
70a9645fc0db5371: AYER KEROH: The issue of machinery import duties allegedly being imposed on local companies despite them securing exemption approvals from the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) will be raised with the Customs Department and the Finance Ministry (MoF).

Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the matter was raised by several industry operators during a dialogue session with the business community in Melaka yesterday.
He said some companies claimed they were forced to pay duties upon despite already possessing exemption approval letters from Mida.
He said there were allegations that such payments could not be refunded even after the exemption status was subsequently clarified.
"This should not be happening. There are several cases like this, and I will be taking this matter up with Customs and MoF.
"If this continues, Mida becomes redundant. Companies come and apply, Mida grants the exemption, yet when the machinery is brought in, they are still made to pay duties," he said.
Johari said such circumstances could adversely affect the cash flow of local companies, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) investing to enhance production efficiency.
"They decided to purchase machinery to improve production efficiency. That is precisely why we grant the exemption.
"I have not yet had the opportunity to examine the documents regarding the issues raised in earlier dialogue.

"However, provide me with the facts and complete details, and I will look into it. If the payments have not been refunded, we need to ask why. For how long will people respect Mida if situations like this occur?"
Johari said it was important that government agencies coordinate matters to ensure that every policy introduced is implemented effectively across all levels of enforcement.
He said dialogue sessions with the business community are vital for identifying policy implementation issues and gathering direct feedback from industry operators.
1a28d65c88c020be: SAO PAULO: Mercedes secured their ninth Formula One constructors' world championship and completed a title double on Sunday in a Sao Paulo Grand Prix won by McLaren's Lando Norris from pole position for the second year in a row.
The title was Mercedes' first constructors' crown since 2021 and came a week after 20-year-old Italian Kimi Antonelli became the youngest drivers' champion with four races to spare in Mexico City.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen finished second, racing from 21st on the grid due to engine penalties, in a race that started and ended in the rain, and teammate Isack Hadjar was third. George Russell was fourth for Mercedes and Antonelli fifth with the fastest lap.

Mercedes had needed to score only three points more than Ferrari to clinch the title and the Italian team never threatened to prolong the fight on a treacherous track with Charles Leclerc seventh and Lewis Hamilton ninth in his 400th race.
"It was a very tough race, very, very tough," said Norris, the 2025 world champion, of his 14th career win and 50th podium as well as his team's first victory since August.

"A lot of challenges today with the conditions and going onto slicks in the wet is always tough, especially when you are pushing for the lead and trying to catch up a little bit," added the Briton, who lost out to Antonelli at the start.
"The main thing today was I kept it cool and didn't make any mistakes and had the pace when I needed to. Nice to be back on the top step and what a place to do it as well."
Norris took the chequered flag, waved by Brazil soccer forward Neymar, 14.602 seconds clear of Verstappen.
Mercedes equalled Williams' nine constructors' championships.

"It was a very strong beginning of the season and that kind of got us over the line. These last few races have been challenging at times, today it was difficult, but overall I'm so proud for the organisation," said team boss Toto Wolff.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri was sixth with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson sandwiched between the Ferrari drivers in eighth after a fine race that saw the New Zealander start third and run in second place for the first five laps.
Nico Hulkenberg took the final point for Audi in a race of spins, slippery moments and changeable conditions. - Reuters
afd07ba6a3e1612f: PETALING JAYA, Nov 9 — As the Korean dining scene in the Klang Valley matures, newcomers are opening our eyes to regional cuisines and more specialised Korean dishes.
Busan Sikdang debuts in Kota Damansara, a quieter area lacking in Korean restaurants when compared to Desa Sri Hartamas, Ampang and Solaris Mont Kiara where Korean eateries are found on every corner.
Their winning item is Busan’s dwaeji gukbap, a soup first made with discarded pork bones given away by American soldiers during the Korean War.
In South Korea’s second most populous city, the labour intensive soup is found everywhere, keeping many warm and said to even fortify women recovering from childbirth.
My first experience with dwaeji gukbap was in its finest form, as a winter warmer to fight the bitter cold and biting wind in Busan.
The place we ended up in to get out of the cold used pig’s head and pig bones to brew the cloudy broth but the slightly strong meat smell wasn’t for the faint-hearted.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Once you add the chives, spicy ‘dadaegi’ paste and salted shrimps, the colour of the broth will change and develop a stronger taste. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
When I tried Busan Sikdang’s Dwaeji-Gukbap (RM25), the contrast was strikingly different; their broth has a cleaner, sweeter flavour, probably because the meat source is different.
You’re taught how to mix the broth: firstly, add the seasoned chives, then dissolve the spicy dadaegi paste and lastly, the salted shrimps.
Since gukbap translates to “rice with soup”, add your bowl of rice to the broth to savour them together.
Even though the flavour is lighter here, I found it easier eat especially with our warmer weather.
Ideally, look for this during peak rainstorm time, as that broth helps keep you warm when the temperature dips.
Select from various toppings to suit your preference: smooth, tender pork belly; strongly flavoured, savoury blood sausage (sundae); or chewy offal.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Look for Busan Sikdang at the row of shophouses where two seafood noodle and chili ‘pan mee’ restaurants are located in Kota Damansara; parking is available at the nearby Sunway Nexis. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
The pork belly slices may have a fat layer but expert cooking converts it to a dreamy melt-in-the-mouth texture.
I like wrapping each piece of the pork belly with their kimchi for extra flavour, then eating it with a spoonful of the soft rice grains and soup.
On the side, the banchan include Medium Jangajji, assorted pickles of radish, onions and chillies combined with soy sauce and sugar, which help cut through the fatty, oily food and meat.
There’s also Kkakdugi or radish kimchi and the usual cabbage kimchi with a mellow flavour.
Once you master dwaeji gukbap and find kimchi jigae too mild for you, you’re ready to unlock expert-level Korean food for a deeper, richer flavour.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Unlock the ultimate level of Korean food with this Kimchi-Jjim, an aged ‘kimchi’ and pork belly stew with a richer, deeper flavour. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
Enter Kimchi-jjim (RM50) — a potent deep, rich flavoured stew — where well-fermented aged kimchi is cooked with pork belly.
That pot can easily feed two people with rice and seaweed.
You won’t be able to stop eating it, as you fold the rice with seaweed and add a piece of the pork with the aged kimchi, which has a silky texture after a long braising time.
No wonder this dish is well known as a “rice thief,” as a carbless diet is discarded once you taste that luscious braised pork, whose fat has tempered the slightly sour kimchi.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Stir-Fried Pork is the kind of dish that will require a second bowl of rice to enjoy the tender sliced pork belly with ‘gochujang’, spices and sliced onions. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi

Stir-fried Pork (RM28) or jeyuk-bokkeum is also another rice killer dish, featuring tender slices of pork belly with spicy, savoury notes from the gochujang, garlic, ginger and a touch of sweetness from sliced onions.
This version is served on a hot plate to keep it warm while you eat it with rice.
Some people order specific dishes in restaurants to test them out; for Korean places, I often test them out with Gyeran Mari (RM18) or Korean egg roll.
Their egg roll may not be super fluffy but it’s still a good companion for the meal with its flecks of vegetables that contrast beautifully with the yellow colour.
There’s also Steamed Egg (RM15) for puffy, fluffy cooked eggs too.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

The best way to enjoy Kimchi-jjim (left) is to place the rice on seaweed with a piece of pork belly and aged ‘kimchi’. Gyeran Mari (right) is a fluffy egg roll flecked with diced vegetables. — Pictures by Lee Khang Yi

e0a7468d01ccb314: Huawei claims it’s built a desktop PC that uses only parts made in CHina.

The company launched the Qingyun HM650 last week and said it uses Huawei’s own Kirin X90 processor, a ten-core 20-thread machine with a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The machine runs a newly developed enterprise version of HarmonyOS, the OS Huawei developed to end its dependence on Android and which it intends to run on most of the devices it makes.

A single Chinese government agency has reportedly signed up for 600 of the machines. That’s not an indication this machine is a curiosity, because Beijing has ordered all government entities to shift from Wintel boxes to local alternatives.

While Huawei has reportedly claimed local companies manufactured 100 percent of the components in the machine, it is unclear if all those components use Chinese designs. The Register mentions that uncertainty as many non-Chinese companies continue to operate factories in China.

Even if Huawei is using some parts that aren’t entirely Chinese, the debut of the Qingyun HM650 is bad news for Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm, as all are suffering as the PC market shrinks due to the rising cost of memory. China’s government is an enormous buyer, and losing the chance to bid for its business is unlikely to be helpful.

Lenovo has not named a new leader for its APAC outpost.

The nation hopes to use the chips to secure storage of the national digital signature certification system, and critical infrastructure systems in electricity, water, oil and gas, and telecommunications.
Hanoi says the chip needs more testing before the government will trust it to protect state secrets, but hailed the chip as an important step towards development of sovereign security capabilities.

07ab4456e86fd35a: KOTA BHARU, Nov 9 — The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia (JBPM) is drawing on its experience in handling the massive 2014 floods to strengthen its preparedness for potential extreme disasters in the state, said its director, Farhan Sufyan Borhan.

Farhan Sufyan said such situations were common in disaster management, particularly during floods, but advance planning and training could help minimise disruption during the initial response phase.
“Coordination among rescue agencies is also crucial to ensuring a swift response and avoiding duplication of efforts,” he said.

c1df8e19bfe0d294: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — The life and legacy of Malaysia’s second Prime Minister, Tun Abdul Razak Hussein, are coming to the screen in a new Astro documentary marking 50 years since his death.

Titled Man Who Walked the Talk: The Tun Razak Story, the documentary offers a closer look at the man widely known as the “Father of Development” (Bapa Pembangunan), whose policies helped shape Malaysia’s education, economy and rural development.

Directed by Ahmad Yazid and Izzy Ani Arope, and produced by Abdul Razak’s son, Tan Sri Nazir Razak, the 62-minute documentary combines archival footage, personal recollections and interviews with those who knew the former leader or witnessed his leadership.

Among those featured are former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, AbdulRazak’s sons Datuk Seri Nizam Razak and Datuk Ahmad Johari Razak, and Datin Kalsom Taib, daughter of the late Tan Sri Taib Andak.
Their accounts offer a more personal portrait of Abdul Razak, shedding light on his character, working relationships and approach to leadership beyond his public image.
View this post on Instagram
A post shared by Astro Gempak (@astrogempak)
The documentary traces his journey from his early years to his rise through Malaysia’s political establishment, exploring the principles and decisions that defined his time in office.
It also revisits some of his most significant policies, particularly those aimed at reducing poverty, improving rural infrastructure and expanding access to education and economic opportunities.

Through archival material and expert perspectives, the film examines the challenges facing Malaysia in its early years as an independent nation and how Abdul Razak’s development priorities helped shape its socioeconomic direction.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Astro’s ‘Man Who Walked the Talk: The Tun Razak Story’ revisits the life and legacy of Malaysia’s second prime minister, marking 50 years since his death. — Picture courtesy of Astro
Born on March 11, 1922, in Pekan, Pahang, Abdul Razak came from an aristocratic family and attended Malay College Kuala Kangsar before continuing his education at Raffles College in Singapore.
He later studied law at Lincoln’s Inn in Britain before returning to Malaya to pursue a career in public service.
His political career saw him serve as Pahang state secretary, acting menteri besar of Pahang, minister of education and deputy prime minister before becoming Malaysia’s second prime minister in 1970.

During his tenure, he made rural development and poverty reduction central to his administration’s agenda, earning a reputation as one of the principal architects of Malaysia’s early development policies.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Through archival footage and personal recollections, the documentary explores Tun Abdul Razak’s role in shaping Malaysia’s development and his enduring legacy. — Picture courtesy of Astro
His premiership was cut short when he died in London on January 14, 1976, aged 53, after suffering from leukaemia.

Five decades later, Man Who Walked the Talk: The Tun Razak Story revisits both his public achievements and the personal convictions that guided his leadership, examining how his legacy continues to resonate in Malaysia today.
The documentary premieres tonight on Astro Ria at 8.30pm, followed by a broadcast on Astro Prima at 9pm.
It will also be available on Astro On Demand and Sooka.
969fc1c1ea4c7f82: HONG KONG: Asian markets and US equity futures made a steady start on Monday, wobbling into positive territory after a wild week where doubts about demand for computer chips sent tech-heavy markets in Asia into some of their steepest falls in years.

1466f03cb6564794: AL AYYAT, Nov 9 — Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital yesterday, derailing several carriages, killing seven people and injuring more than 100 others, according to the authorities.
Egypt’s railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan.
The health ministry said 112 people were injured and were now being treated in hospitals around the Giza area.
The ministry said the injuries ranged from bruises and abrasions to fractures of the limbs, pelvis and vertebrae, as well as head and facial lacerations and chest injuries.
Forty-five patients had been discharged after receiving treatment, while seven others were expected to be released later.

President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was following the accident “with great concern”, and had directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to “hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent”.
Witnesses described chaotic rescue efforts after the collision, as villagers, first responders and railway workers scrambled to reach passengers trapped inside overturned carriages.
Abdel Wahed Mohamed, 31, who was sitting at a nearby cafe when the collision occurred, said the Aswan-bound train had stopped, when the Fayoum-bound train crashed into it.
“The train overturned at around 1:30 pm. Six carriages overturned,” he said, adding that victims suffered a range of injuries, including head wounds and broken limbs.
Another witness, Ahmed Moussa, 25, said rescuers dug beneath one overturned carriage to reach trapped passengers.
“There were people piled on top of each other inside,” he said, adding that he saw two women among the dead.
Taha Abdel Tawab, 43, said he “saw a young man leaving the train carrying his dead father”.
AFP journalists saw several passenger carriages strewn across the tracks and surrounding farmland.
One carriage lay on its side beside the railway embankment, while another had been torn open by the force of the impact, exposing twisted metal, shattered seats and passengers’ belongings.
Heavy machinery
Rescue workers used cranes and heavy machinery to right overturned carriages as ambulances ferried the injured to nearby hospitals.
Villagers gathered around the cordoned-off wreckage, watching recovery operations continue into the evening.
One victim was a resident of the nearby village, according to local witness Reda Kamel Labib, who criticised rescue delays caused by inadequate transport infrastructure in the area.
First responders and passersby helped lift one of the victims out of the wreckage in a black body bag, AFP images showed.
Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza’s Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt’s worst-ever rail disaster.
In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holiday travellers south of Cairo.
In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens.
Egypt’s 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the network — one of the largest in Africa — has suffered repeated deadly accidents.

Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network. — AFP
9178fdd9021d64e3: BERLIN: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Sunday he intended to appoint Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner as the country's next president, in 2027, making her the first woman in the post.
He made his announcement at a dinner for leaders of his centre-right CDU party, confirming information leaked last week by party sources.
Aigner, 61, belongs to the CSU, the Bavarian sister party of the CDU.
Aigner's nomination by Merz virtually guarantees her election on Jan 30, as those voting are almost all drawn from Germany's two parliamentary chambers.
Currently speaker of the southern state's regional assembly, she would replace outgoing President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, a Social Democrat, in the largely ceremonial post.
Steinmeier, who took office in 2017, will reach the limit of two five-year terms in March 2027.
German political practice is that coalition parties agree on a common candidate for the job. The president is meant to be above party politics, representing the moral conscience of the country.
The current ruling coalition is made up of the CDU, the CSU and the Social Democrats of the SPD.
The SPD has frequently voiced its support for Aigner as president.
During the chancellorship of Angela Merkel, she served as agriculture minister, winning the respect of politicians outside her own party.
Dietmar Woidke, one regional SPD leader, told the news website Politico that she would be the "perfect candidate" for the job.
"She knows German politics like the back of her hand," he said. "She's accessible. She likes people, knows how to listen and people listen to her," he added.
Her appearances in traditional dress at Germany's beer festivals have also helped raise her profile in Bavaria.
And her way of dealing with the far-right AfD party in the Bavarian regional parliament is admired for being both firm and courteous.
At a time of increased political polarisation, and as the anti-migrant, pro-Russian AfD is registering a record 28 per cent in opinion polls, her admirers see her as a potential calming influence.
Aigner was born in Bavaria to parents who ran an electricity company. She survived a brush with cancer in her youth, when a tumour had to be removed from her back.
After technical studies, she worked as an electronics technician with a helicopter builder before moving into local and then federal politics.--AFP
7a91e26c472e4126: FOR years, Paraguay's digital bank, Ueno, stood out as a homegrown success story, luring roughly half the country's people to open accounts and offering many the opportunity to hold a bank account for the very first time.

But over just five days this week, the bank collapsed, freezing the savings of nearly three million customers — in a country of 6.5 million people — and triggering the country's deepest political crisis in more than a decade.
On Friday evening, President Santiago Pena was impeached after attempting to resign, and his vice president, Pedro Alliana, was sworn in as his replacement.
Authorities quickly arrested Pena, an economist and close ally of US President Donald Trump, and prosecutors charged him on Saturday with breach of trust and administration for personal gain.
A judge ordered him held in pretrial detention at a military facility.
Pena has denied wrongdoing and his attorney, Ricardo Preda, told journalists that he was pleading not guilty to the charges.
The scandal has triggered public protests and sharp rebukes from the opposition.
"We are facing the biggest corruption scandal in our democratic history," said opposition Senator Rafael Filizzola on Friday.
"This impeachment is a first step toward ensuring justice is served."
Manuel Ferreira, a Paraguayan economist and former finance minister, echoed much of the public anger over the case.
"This was a modern-day Bonnie and Clyde," he said.
"They didn't rob us with a pistol, they robbed us with an app. The head of the gang was the president of the republic."
Until March 2025, Pena had been a business partner of the group that owns ueno. After his election in 2023, he tapped Ueno's former president, Carlos Carvallo, to lead the central bank.
Carvallo resigned as central bank chief earlier this week. Prosecutors charged him on Saturday with breach of trust, producing false public documents and administration for personal gain.
They sought his pretrial detention, which was approved by a judge.
Carvallo did not respond to a request for comment. It was not immediately clear if he had entered a plea in the case.
Pena's lawyer, Preda, objected to the impeachment, saying that ousting a president during a bank resolution could itself be destabilising.
"What sets a serious country apart is not that its banks don't fail, but how it responds," Preda said on Friday.
"If there is one thing that undermines confidence in the financial system, it is attempting to oust the president without evidence."
Ueno was launched in 2021 as a sleek, millennial-friendly banking app that quickly won over Paraguayans who had been underserved by brick-and-mortar institutions.
It soon became deeply embedded in Paraguay's payments system. It paired its digital offering with physical branches, later sponsoring sports teams, businesses and events.
As of June, public institutions — including Paraguay's state pension fund — held roughly US$850 million in accounts with the bank.

But in recent months, internal regulatory reports warning of excessive lending to certain companies were leaked to local media outlets ABC and Última Hora, triggering political scrutiny of the bank's lending practices.

Following growing public pressure, Paraguay's central bank on Tuesday put ueno into resolution — its strongest measure ‌short of immediate liquidation — after determining that Ueno had breached minimum solvency requirements, locking ​millions of customers temporarily out of their accounts.
The central bank said on Saturday that the equivalent of US$160 million had since been paid out to nearly 1.2 million savers under the state deposit guarantee scheme.

Authorities have promised that depositors will be reimbursed and say the crisis is confined to Ueno. But analysts say the damage to Paraguay's reputation as a stable investment destination in South America may linger far longer than the bank resolution itself.
"This is the moment when Paraguay must demonstrate that its institutions are functioning," Ferreira said.

On October 14, the High Court dismissed Najib’s application to stay the execution of his 15-year prison sentence and RM11.38 billion fine in the 1MDB case pending his appeal.
The big ‘if’ did not materialize. Najib was not granted a stay of his 15-year 1MDB sentence.

Accordingly the AGC has reason to say that Najib’s house arrest “needed to be examined in light of the High Court’s rejection on October 14, 2026 of [his] application for a stay of execution of his sentence in the 1MDB case”.
The matter is, if not “legally complex”, rightly unprecedented.
I would humbly agree that a “clear and definitive legal clarification was necessary before any further implementation action could be taken”.

The Attorney General has a variety of different responsibilities. Under the Constitution, he is not only the government’s chief legal adviser; he is the chief legal adviser to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

It is the Attorney General’s duty under Article 145(3) of the Federal Constitution to advise the Yang di-Pertuan Agong “upon such legal matters” and to discharge the functions conferred on him by or under this Constitution or any other written law.
The execution of Najib’s house arrest is such a legal matter.

Lord Goldsmith, who served as the Attorney General for England and Wales and Attorney General for Northern Ireland from June 8, 2001, to June 27, 2007, under Prime Minister Tony Blair, once considered that “upholding the Rule of Law” was one of his key functions as Attorney General. He identified this role as “most obviously my role as the Government’s chief legal adviser, although it goes wider”. Upholding the rule of law is about compliance with the law.

So, let’s give space to Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar to advise the Yang di-Pertuan Agong as he seeks an audience with His Majesty to discuss Najib’s house arrest in his SRC International case.
Let the Attorney General advise the Yang di-Pertuan Agong upon such a legal matter.

dff146cd141d1370: PARIS: From 24-hour news channel parodies and extreme stereotypes to a twisted Statue of Liberty, the Grand Theft Auto series has consistently mocked the excesses of US capitalist society.

But with days to go before the release of the hugely popular video game's new instalment, players and analysts are wondering if changes in studio Rockstar's creative team suggest a possible shift into less controversial territory, and an end to the punk-rock transgressions that helped turn GTA into a cultural phenomenon.

In marketing and communications leading up to the release of the new "GTA VI" on Nov 19, Rockstar seems keener to steer the conversation toward its Bonnie-and-Clyde-style protagonists trying to survive in a fictionalised, crime-ravaged Miami.

"It's a valid question," said expert Olivier Mauco, author of the book "GTA IV, the Dark Side of the American Dream", noting the various presentations of the new game had so far put the franchise's famed political incorrectness "much less front and centre."

Looking for an explanation for the possible toning-down, Chris Klippel, founder of the specialist outlet Rockstar Mag, noted that "of the five writers who worked on GTA V, three have left," including Dan Houser, one of the two brothers who founded the studio.
"So that inevitably raises concerns."
For expert Christopher Dring, GTA's "punk rock" style is part of Rockstar's DNA.
"That's the whole idea behind them. They know they're middle fingers to the establishment.
"They like making cultural moments. They like people talking about them. They won't play it safe, and if they do, it will be disappointing."
- Criticism and controversy -
GTA's taste for transgression goes back to the very first instalment, in 1997.
"To get people talking about them and come across as the bad boys of the industry, the Houser brothers made it seem like GTA was encouraging kids to steal cars," said Mauco.
The bad-boy reputation stuck to the series, which has been regularly accused of glorifying violence and inciting criminal behaviour, even as it became a symbol of rebellious culture.
Starting with "Vice City" (2002) and "San Andreas" (2004), Rockstar gradually began weaving social issues into its gangster stories.

The turning point came with "GTA IV", released in 2008, which features a protagonist — an immigrant from Eastern Europe — trapped in a spiral of violence as he confronts the flip side of the American dream.
"It's certainly the most thoroughly written in terms of social critique," said Mauco.
"It's practically an auteur game, which is pretty wild and paradoxical because even back then it was already one of the most expensive games ever developed."
- Walking a tightrope -
Released in 2013, the next instalment, "GTA V", involves a microcosm of US class warfare with stereotypes on both sides: left-leaning urbane hipsters pitted against Midwestern rednecks.
For Mauco, it portrayed "an America that no longer talks to itself", three years before Donald Trump won the White House.
Although the game has since sold more than 230 million copies, it is difficult to gauge how much gamers cared about its political message.
A lot of GTA's players "are mostly there to blow off steam" and unleash chaos in these vast fictional metropolises, said Klippel.
"I still think it's going to remain very satirical — that's the whole appeal of the series," said Dring, an expert for specialist outlet The Game Business.
Dring compared GTA's biting humour to that of the cartoon "South Park", and warned against expecting direct attacks on Trump or Russia in "GTA VI."
He predicted instead "a critical look at culture and society", starting with the omnipresence of social media.
"GTA has always managed to find the right balance: a world that invites escapism while poking fun at the problems of the modern world."
A thorny tightrope to walk if the game wants to avoid being accused of having a political agenda — a major no-no for many of its biggest fans.

720ee294ff4a7df1: NOVEMBER 9 — A small business can be busy every day and still struggle to make ends meet. Customers arrive, orders keep coming, and sales appear encouraging. Yet after paying suppliers, rent, utilities and other expenses, the owner may discover that very little remains. The business is operating, but is it actually becoming stronger?

This question deserves attention following the announcement of Malaysia’s Budget 2027 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on 9 October. For micro and small entrepreneurs facing financial pressures, government assistance can provide much-needed opportunities. However, beyond the amount allocated, a more important question emerges: can today’s financial support create businesses that remain sustainable tomorrow?

Budget 2027 includes RM6.6 billion in microfinancing and RM200 million under Sejahtera MADANI grants, with the latter targeting 40,000 recipients, particularly women, for equipment and training assistance. These initiatives recognise the financial and resource constraints that can prevent entrepreneurs from improving their operations.

For a food seller, better equipment could reduce wastage. For a tailor, an efficient sewing machine could increase production. For a neighbourhood retailer, additional working capital could help maintain inventory. Such improvements matter, particularly when limited resources restrict business development.
But does receiving more capital necessarily mean becoming financially stronger?

Consider a small restaurant that obtains financing to expand its operations. Sales may increase, but so might operating expenses. Without proper pricing, cost management and cash flow planning, the owner could end up working harder without earning significantly more.

This illustrates an important economic distinction. Business growth and business sustainability are related, but they are not identical. Higher revenue does not automatically translate into greater profitability, while years of operation do not necessarily guarantee financial resilience.
The challenge, therefore, is not simply helping entrepreneurs access financing, but ensuring they can convert that financing into lasting improvements.

Micro and small businesses also have different needs. A home-based entrepreneur may require basic equipment and practical guidance, while an established retailer may benefit more from inventory management, financial planning or access to new markets. Assistance becomes more meaningful when it responds to these differences rather than assuming every business faces similar challenges.

Digitalisation offers another example. Technology can simplify transactions, improve inventory monitoring and support business decisions. However, introducing digital tools should not become an achievement in itself. A retailer accepting digital payments may enjoy greater convenience, but without understanding daily expenses and profit margins, the business may remain financially vulnerable.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

The author argues that entrepreneurship support should be judged not by funding distributed, but by whether businesses become more profitable, resilient and less dependent on repeated assistance. — Pexels pic
Technology creates value when it improves business performance, not merely when it is adopted.

The same principle applies to entrepreneurship training. Someone who has operated a business for ten years may not need another introductory course on starting a business. Instead, practical guidance on pricing, managing cash flow, controlling costs and preparing for unexpected disruptions could be more valuable.

This raises an important consideration for entrepreneurship policy. Financing approvals, equipment distribution and training participation indicate how widely programmes reach entrepreneurs. However, these measures alone cannot establish whether the businesses receiving assistance have become more sustainable.

A stronger assessment would examine what happens afterwards. Have profit margins improved? Are entrepreneurs managing their finances more effectively? Can their businesses withstand weaker demand or unexpected expenses? Are they becoming less dependent on repeated financial assistance?
These questions do not diminish the importance of government support. Rather, they help determine whether public resources are creating lasting economic value.

Importantly, sustainability should not be confused with rapid expansion. Not every hawker dreams of opening multiple outlets, and not every home-based entrepreneur wants to establish a large company. For many, success means earning a stable income, supporting their families and operating without constant financial uncertainty.

One practical approach is to complement financing with needs-based mentoring, simple financial management tools and periodic business assessments. Such support could help entrepreneurs identify operational weaknesses, strengthen decision-making and build resilience beyond the initial assistance period.

Budget 2027 offers an opportunity to strengthen Malaysia’s micro and small enterprises. Its longer-term significance, however, should be considered not only through how much assistance is announced, but also through the improvements businesses achieve and sustain.

For the entrepreneur opening the shop tomorrow morning, financial assistance may provide welcome breathing space. But the greater achievement would be building a business where every unexpected expense no longer threatens another month of survival.
Because the real measure of entrepreneurship support is not simply how many businesses it helps remain open today, but how many become strong enough to face tomorrow with greater confidence.

133fd40526098176: ROME, Nov 9 — Inter Milan claimed a statement 2-0 win over Como on Sunday to move just one point behind Serie A leaders Lazio, who were held to a 1-1 draw at Napoli.

Francesco Pio Esposito and Marcus Thuram struck in the opening 20 minutes as Inter ended a six-match winning run from Como that included the biggest away win in Champions League history, Wednesday’s 9-1 demolition of French side Lens.

Inter, who suffered their first league defeat of the season to rivals AC Milan a week ago, jumped back into second as a thrilling title race heats up, with two points separating Lazio from third-placed Roma.
“Today we played well in every aspect. We put pressure on their build-up and accepted that they could cause us problems,” said Inter coach Cristian Chivu.
“We counter-attacked with ferocity and were clinical in front of goal. I applaud my players for a performance of maturity and quality.”
Cesc Fabregas’ Como were outclassed in defeat at San Siro, allowing Milan to leapfrog them into fourth on 24 points after Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic struck in a 2-1 win over Genoa.
Inter made a fast start as they looked to put the memory of last weekend’s Milan derby defeat behind them, Esposito tapping in an inviting Djed Spence cross after 12 minutes.
They soon made it two when a poor clearance dropped invitingly into Thuram’s path in the box and the France international lashed a shot past Robert Sanchez.

Como mustered little in response in an uncharacteristically muted display as Federico Dimarco and Thuram threatened a third with efforts in the second half, before Nico Paz clipped the crossbar late on.
Lazio stumble, Milan react
Leaders Lazio dropped points for just the second time this season at struggling Napoli as Davide Frattesi’s opener was cancelled out by an Alfonso Pedraza own goal.
Napoli were under pressure to deliver a result after defeats by Juventus and Porto saw the squad sent into a training retreat in a bid to revive their flagging form.
But they could only claim a point against Gennaro Gattuso’s unbeaten outfit, whose remarkable form continued as they remained 14 points ahead of 10th-placed Napoli.
“We must keep going, everything’s not lost even if we are behind in the standings,” Napoli coach Massimiliano Allegri said.
Milan finished a mixed week on a high as a second Serie A win on the bounce took them into the top four.
Ruben Amorim’s side impressed with their 3-1 Milan derby win last weekend, but inconsistency reared its head again with a 2-0 Europa League loss at home to Ferencvaros on Thursday.
Amorim was left furious by his side’s performance in that game but saw a much-improved start from his players at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris.
Cisse swept in the opener after 13 minutes before Pulisic doubled their lead six minutes later, and Mikael Ellertsson’s late strike for Genoa proved no more than a consolation.
Juve’s troubles continue
Juventus lost more ground as they twice fought back to claim a 2-2 draw with Fiorentina in Florence.
The result left Luciano Spalletti’s side seventh with 18 points, while Fiorentina moved two points clear of the relegation zone on nine points.

Mateo Pellegrino headed Fiorentina in front from a corner after just four minutes, but Juventus levelled when Randal Kolo Muani cut in from the right wing and teed up strike partner Nick Woltemade for his first Serie A goal.

Alieu Njie restored the hosts’ lead early in the second half with his third goal in three games after a goalmouth scramble, but Juve responded when some uncertain goalkeeping from David de Gea allowed Gleison Bremer to head a corner into an unguarded net.
Guglielmo Vicario produced two big saves in the dying minutes as Fiorentina tried in vain to take the lead for a third time.
Atalanta ended a six-match winless run in all competitions by beating Monza 1-0 thanks to a Nikola Krstovic strike. — AFP
