de0f7054d90e62e7: NOVEMBER 9 — In many Asian households, parents do not need to raise their voices to express disappointment. A single look is enough. The raised eyebrow, narrowed eyes and long, silent stare can deliver an entire lecture. Asian parents deserve an award for communicating through eye language alone!

Now, imagine placing a report card in those very hands. One glance at the grades, followed by another at the child, and the interrogation begins. “What happened here?” “Why is this subject so low?” “What does your friend’s result look like?” Apparently, a report card is never just a report card. It is a family event, complete with a review session nobody volunteered to attend.

For children growing up in the 1990s, getting a parent’s signature required military-level preparation. The bedroom became a rehearsal room. Possible questions received carefully prepared answers, and excuses underwent several rounds of editing. Even household chores suddenly became attractive. Washing dishes, sweeping floors and folding clothes without being asked were excellent strategies for securing a peaceful negotiation.

Unfortunately, no amount of preparation guaranteed success. The report card still needed a signature, and the teacher needed to receive it. Some students became experts at delaying submission, remaining the last in class to return their cards. A few even considered signing the document themselves. The imagination was brave, but the actual hand remained frozen. For a typical 1990s child, the consequences of forging a parent’s signature were simply too terrifying!

Fast-forward to adulthood, and look who is holding the paperwork now. The same children who once trembled at report cards have become unofficial health inspectors, examining their parents’ blood pressure, blood sugar and cholesterol readings. The former examiners are now the examinees, and their children have taken over the questioning. “Did you take your medicine?” “When was your last check-up?” “What did the doctor say?”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The author argues that as children grow older, caring for ageing parents becomes a role reversal rooted in patience, practical support and enduring family love. — Pexels pic

Somewhere along the way, the family report-card system has undergone a major upgrade. Unfortunately, the new subjects are considerably more serious, and there is no school holiday after the examination.

Yet convincing parents to take their health seriously can feel harder than explaining a disappointing examination result. A high sugar reading comes with a defence. A worrying blood pressure reading comes with an explanation. A doctor’s advice comes with a counterargument. Parents who once expected children to accept instructions without debate suddenly become expert lawyers when their own health is involved! Ask them to take a neighbourhood walk, and the excuses arrive faster than food delivery.
“Very tired today.”
“Already doing housework.”
“Tomorrow lah!”

Apparently, sweeping, gardening, cooking and folding laundry qualify as a complete fitness programme. The irony is difficult to miss. These are the same parents who insisted that discipline mattered, excuses were unacceptable and tomorrow was not an answer. Now, their adult children deliver the very lectures they once dreaded hearing.

Perhaps it is time to retire the lecture and try a little family diplomacy. Instead of repeatedly asking, “Did you check your sugar level?”, why not make Monday an unofficial family health-check day? A glucometer, used with proper guidance, can help parents monitor their blood sugar when advised to do so. A quick update in the family WhatsApp group might become as routine as sending a good-morning sticker. Of course, readings need proper interpretation, and concerning results should be discussed with a healthcare professional.

The real challenge is getting everyone involved without making the family chat resemble a hospital waiting room. A cheerful “Monday health report, everyone!” might receive a warmer response than “Ma, Pa, why haven’t you checked your sugar?” Nobody enjoys feeling inspected during every conversation.

Exercise deserves the same change of strategy. Telling parents to walk every evening is easy; getting them out of the house is another matter. Rather than issuing instructions from the sofa, adult children could put on their walking shoes and join them. Start with a short stroll, exchange family gossip and discuss dinner. Before long, walking may become less about exercise and more about spending time together. If the weather is bad, there is always another opportunity, provided “tomorrow lah” does not become a permanent family tradition!

Of course, family health management also involves appointments, medication refills and medical reports. A shared calendar and organised folder can prevent last-minute panic when searching for prescriptions or remembering check-up dates. More importantly, responsibility should not fall on one child alone. Caring for ageing parents is a family affair, not a one-person administrative department.

Still, even the most organised family cannot turn health into a perfectly controlled examination. Parents have their own preferences, habits and fears. Some worry about receiving bad news; others are simply tired of being told what to do. Concern is understandable, but so is the desire for independence. The trick is knowing when to remind, when to listen and when to let a conversation breathe.

Perhaps growing up is not simply about earning a salary, paying bills or becoming independent. Sometimes, it means recognising that the people who once held our hands now need us to hold theirs. One day, someone checks a school report; years later, someone reads a medical report, hoping the numbers are reassuring.

As children, many of us wanted rainbow colours across our report cards, hoping every achievement would earn a smile of approval. Today, we look at our parents’ medical reports with a different kind of hope. We may not expect perfect numbers, but we want enough good news for another family meal, festive celebration, birthday photograph and ordinary afternoon together.

The paperwork has changed, the questions have changed and the roles have reversed. Yet, beneath the reminders, WhatsApp messages and occasional family arguments lies the same old wish: for the people we love to be around a little longer. Perhaps that is the one result no report card can measure.

e8542434ac251449: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 9 — Penang police said an 11-year-old girl allegedly sexually abused by her father was placed in her paternal grandmother’s temporary care on Oct 16, the day he was arrested and remanded, and handed to her mother on Oct 21, three days before his remand ended.

Penang Chief Police Officer Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the girl’s school principal lodged a report with the Criminal Investigation Division of the Southwest District Police Headquarters at 11.15 am on Oct 16, and the suspect was arrested at about 5.30 pm that day and remanded until Oct 24.

“The girl was referred to the One Stop Crisis Centre (OSCC) at Penang Hospital on Oct 17 and remained in the paediatric ward until Oct 21, when the Southwest District Social Welfare Department (JKM) handed her to her biological mother,” he said in a statement tonight.
Lim said the girl was initially placed in her grandmother’s temporary care because her biological mother was in Singapore at the time.
He said the suspect was charged at the Balik Pulau Court on Oct 24 under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, read together with Section 16 of the same Act.

“The case is still being tried, with the next court mention scheduled for Nov 11, 2026,” he said and advised the public against speculating or spreading unverified information that could cause misunderstanding about the case.

The statement came following remarks by Berapit state assemblyman Heng Lee Lee in a news report last Thursday questioning the decision to allow the girl to return to a home allegedly shared with the suspect instead of being placed under immediate protection.

Heng urged the Social Welfare Department to adopt a more compassionate, flexible and responsive approach when handling vulnerable children, and called for seamless coordination among welfare officers, medical personnel and police. — Bernama

0cc30211284325f7: ASUNCION: Police in Paraguay raided the home of ex-president Santiago Pena as part of a probe into a banking crisis that triggered his dismissal from office and criminal charges against him.
Authorities last week intervened to seize Ueno Bank, a popular online lender that held accounts for nearly half of Paraguay's 6.5 million people, plus more than US$800 million in government funds.
Its collapse rocked this small, normally stable country, leading to street protests. Pena is now being held in custody at a military facility.
Pena, who came to power in 2023, owned shares in the bank's holding company, Ueno Holding, until he sold them last year.

He is accused of using his influence as president to steer millions in government deposits to Ueno Bank and of hiding or downplaying its financial woes even though he was warned about questionable loans and solvency issues.
Prosecutors announced in a statement that Pena's home was raided as part of the probe into the bank collapse.
They say Ueno Bank received deposits from government entities even as it granted questionable loans to companies linked to Ueno executives.
Pena's mansion outside Asuncion is part of the probe. The indictment says that in 2024 he received two loans from Ueno Bank totaling around US$500,000 so he could build the house.
His monthly mortgage payment is US$38,000 – six times his monthly salary as president, the charging sheet says.
The Senate voted Friday to dismiss Pena, and Vice President Pedro Alliana took his place.
Alliana said Sunday the government has reimbursed 1.2 million Ueno Bank customers whose money was frozen in the collapse.
The disbursal totals around US$158 million so far, and it will continue this week, he said. - AFP PIC

83201735754a2f68: DOHA, Nov 9 — Malaysia has emphasised the need to strengthen cybersecurity and child online protection while ensuring the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies.

Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said trust and safety were essential to enabling people to participate confidently in the digital economy, as technological advancements continued to reshape the way people lived and worked.
He said innovation must be accompanied by appropriate safeguards to protect users and build public confidence in digital technologies.
“The Declaration rightly puts a strong focus on cybersecurity, protecting children online, and ensuring that emerging technologies are developed and used responsibly.

“For Malaysia, innovation must go hand in hand with the right safeguards. This will give people the confidence to make full use of the opportunities that digital technologies offer,” he said at the Ministerial Roundtable held in conjunction with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference 2026 (PP-26), here today.
Fahmi said Malaysia welcomed the draft Doha Ministerial Declaration, which outlined a comprehensive approach to addressing the opportunities and challenges of digital transformation.

He said the declaration reflected three priorities central to Malaysia’s national digital agenda, which were ensuring meaningful connectivity, promoting digital inclusion and fostering a safe and trusted digital environment.
He said meaningful connectivity must go beyond network coverage to ensure that telecommunications services remain affordable, reliable and resilient in supporting communities and economic activities.

Malaysia also welcomed the declaration’s emphasis on developing resilient and sustainable digital infrastructure to ensure the continuity of essential communications during emergencies and disruptions.
Fahmi said digital transformation must create opportunities for everyone regardless of geographical location or level of digital readiness.
He added that the Malaysian government remained focused on investing in digital skills and capacity building while supporting innovation to enable more people to benefit from the digital economy.
“As AI and other emerging technologies continue to develop, we must make sure that developing countries and underserved communities are not left behind.
“They should have the opportunity not only to use these technologies, but also to help shape them and benefit from the opportunities they create,” he said.

Fahmi also welcomed the declaration’s emphasis on international cooperation and acknowledged the ITU’s important role in expanding connectivity, developing technical standards and strengthening digital capacity.

He said Malaysia looked forward to working closely with the ITU and other member states to build a more connected and inclusive digital future while ensuring greater safety and equitable opportunities for all. — Bernama

af0c6d3a3a738d95: DOHA: Malaysia is considering accelerating its quantum migration process to strengthen national data security amid advances in quantum computing technology that are expected to pose new challenges to cybersecurity systems.

Communications minister Fahmi Fadzil said he had asked the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to hold discussions with the National Security Council (MKN), the National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) and telecommunications companies to explore potential collaboration in this area.
Fahmi said the collaboration would involve establishing a research and development space to facilitate faster and more secure quantum migration in Malaysia.

“Malaysia is considering accelerating its quantum migration process. I have asked MCMC to engage with the NSC and Nacsa and discuss with telecommunications companies on how we can work together to establish an R&D space for faster and more secure quantum migration,” he said.

Quantum migration refers to the process of upgrading existing digital security systems to adopt quantum-resistant encryption technologies designed to protect data against potential threats from future quantum computers.
Fahmi was commenting on technological innovations that could benefit Malaysia after visiting several exhibition booths at the Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026 yesterday.
He said one of the technological innovations that caught his attention was quantum-safe communication, which is becoming increasingly important for future data protection.
He said the emergence of quantum computers on the market was expected to pose significant challenges to existing cryptography and encryption methods used to safeguard data.
“I foresee that quantum migration and quantum-safe communication will be among the key issues facing many countries in the years ahead.
“Quantum computers are expected to enter the market in the near future, posing major challenges to existing cryptography and encryption methods used to ensure our data remains secure,” he said.

Apart from quantum technology, he said his visit to the exhibition booths also provided an opportunity to explore various innovations, including the integration of artificial intelligence into smart city services and security systems.
d0afb00f98f3a623: KOTA BHARU, Nov 9 — Floods are expected in nine districts in Kelantan from Sunday until Wednesday (Nov 11), following a continuous rain warning issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).

The National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (PRABN) of the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) said the districts are Kota Bharu, Tumpat, Bachok, Machang, Pasir Mas, Pasir Puteh, Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai and Jeli.

It said the preliminary flood forecast followed a Continuous Rain Warning (Alert) issued by MetMalaysia at 4.30pm today, with flood hotspots, low-lying areas and other flood-prone locations expected to be affected.

“In Kota Bharu, areas at risk are located within the Kelantan River Basin, while in Tumpat, they are within the Golok River Basin, covering Sungai Golok, Sungai Pengkalan Nangka, Sungai Mentua and Sungai Kelaboran,” it said in a statement tonight.
In Bachok, areas at risk are within the Kemasin River Basin, including Sungai Jelawat, Sungai Kemasin, Saliran PKS, Saliran KADA drainage and Sungai Bator.
The Semerak River Basin, covering Sungai Lubuk Nibong, Sungai Melor, Sungai Gunong and Sungai Semerak, is also at risk of flooding.
In Machang, areas at risk are within the Kelantan River Basin, including Sungai Kelantan, Sungai Kerawang, Sungai Kweng Hitam and watercourses in Machang town.
In Pasir Mas, flooding is forecast in the Golok River Basin, including Sungai Golok and Sungai Lemal, while in Pasir Puteh, the areas at risk are within the Semerak River Basin.

Areas at risk in Tanah Merah are within the Kelantan River Basin; Sungai Lebir and Sungai Galas, both part of the same basin in Kuala Krai; Sungai Pergau and Sungai Jeli in the Kelantan River Basin, as well as Sungai Lanas in the Golok River Basin in Jeli.
PRABN warned that flooding could occur earlier or later than the forecast period.
Residents, particularly those in flood-prone areas, are advised to remain vigilant and comply with instructions from the authorities.
The public can obtain the latest flood updates through the Public InfoBanjir website at https://publicinfobanjir.water.gov.my/. — Bernama

fcbff09be80281d7: A lot of anger has arisen since Najib Razak was returned to Kajang prison (barely 3km from my own residence in Simpang Balak), after Umno paid the RM50 million fine imposed as part of his sentence in the SRC International case.
Some of that anger came from Umno and its Perikatan Nasional supporters, and some from the office of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

To all and sundry, the royal pardon order was simple enough: once Najib has paid the RM50 million fine, take him back to his Langgak Duta mansion until August 2028, when his sentence in the SRC International case ends.

After that, I presume Najib would then be returned to Kajang prison to serve his 15-year sentence in the 1MDB case and pay his RM11 billion fine. I also assume Umno would then petition for a full pardon, or a partial one with yet another bout of house arrest.

But is this as straightforward as it sounds? There are several issues worth contemplating, as the issue of Najib’s house arrest has set a new precedent. We need to know, and grow from this uncertain prison situation.

My first question is about security. How secure is house arrest, in terms of converting a residence or mansion into a secure facility from an architectural perspective? Does the house need to be renovated with different locks and steel grilles on the windows, so that the prisoner is not able to escape with outside help?
Paying the bill

The more important aspect is: who pays the bill for house repairs and renovation? It is, after all, Najib’s house, and any repairs to it will benefit the owner. The government is only a temporary owner until Najib completes his prison sentence. After that, it is his house once again.
But, of course, he has to go back to Kajang prison in August 2028, unless Umno once again holds the prime minister’s post, as it will make sure of a third or fourth pardon session.

My second question is about visiting arrangements, since the house in Langgak Duta is now gazetted as a prison. As I understand the instructions of the pardons board, without having read the minutes, it calls for just a change of venue.
The question to which all of us are waiting to hear the answer is what the conditions will be at this prison.

Will Najib be able to entertain visits from family members, and Umno or PN members more loosely, and in private so that he can engineer his comeback? Can he access electronic communications to post selfies while eating, reading and exercising lightly, and become the latest YouTube sensation with Bossku 2.0?
Or is Najib subject to the same conditions as he was in Kajang prison?
Who made donations?

A third question about the way donations were made to pay the RM50 million fine. As the amount collected is so large, it sets a precedent of its own: no sane person would believe it came from ordinary members or those sympathising with Najib's situation.

It has been suggested that certain people were responsible for the "donation” that suddenly materialised in a single day, when no one had even guessed that it could happen. We only heard Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki announce that RM10 million was collected within the first two weeks, and then silence. After that, boom, RM50 million was collected!
There have also been concerns that the donations could be some kind of “investment”, or even kickbacks from Umno cronies. This brings into question the morality of the donation..

Although no law requires a donation drive to be audited, I assume it could be done if someone were to make a police or MACC report. But if none comes forth to lodge any reports, then we need a law that says there can be no hanky-panky in donation drives, in order to have some sense of palatable morality regarding the case.
This situation is a first and thus needs some scrutiny.
A matter of morality

An additional concern is regarding the religious implication of making donations to a convicted felon. From a simple search online, I found that a religious fatwa was made stating that a Muslim can donate to help a clearly convicted felon - with the clear condition that he or she admits to the crime and pronounces repentance in public. Then, and only then, is it permissible to help the prisoner.
Since Najib has not fulfilled the religious condition of repentance, as far as I know, where does that leave this country’s Islamic moral compass?
My final question is for whoever is going to lead this country.
One political party is known for having among its ranks people who have been indicted for corruption - not only several members, but also its highest-ranking member and president himself.

It would be to the advantage of future prime ministers, ministers and officials that the house arrest issue be clarified in a crystal clear manner, because the same leaders holding high office could then use this “facility” should their possible indictment occur under a future government.

I therefore applaud the Attorney-General's Chambers and the home minister for taking the unpopular stance of caution before setting this new national precedent. After the coming general election, and when GE17 then comes around, there may be a new government in place, and this issue of house arrest may once again be the fate of many more leaders who transgress their oath of office and religious morality.
Alas, as the saying goes, what goes around eventually comes around.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
2d38583137084e96: Ketegangan berpanjangan di Asia Barat sekali lagi mendedahkan Malaysia kepada risiko bekalan tenaga. Sebarang gangguan bekalan boleh meningkatkan kos pengangkutan dan pengeluaran, sebelum kesannya dirasai rakyat.

Dalam keadaan ini, keputusan kerajaan memperluas Program Biodiesel Negara menerusi peningkatan kadar adunan biodiesel daripada B10 kepada B15 merupakan langkah tepat bagi mengurangkan kebergantungan kepada diesel petroleum.

Kerajaan pada April bersetuju meningkatkan kadar adunan secara berperingkat, bermula dengan B12 sebelum pelaksanaan B15 pada Jun. Bahan api B15 mengandungi 15% biodiesel berasaskan sawit atau palm methyl ester (PME), manakala selebihnya diesel petroleum.
Langkah ini memberi kelebihan kepada Malaysia yang mempunyai industri sawit kukuh serta kemudahan pengeluaran biodiesel sendiri.
Menurut Kementerian Perladangan dan Komoditi (KPK), negara mempunyai 19 loji biodiesel berlesen yang membekalkan PME kepada 34 depot pengadunan di seluruh negara.

Rangkaian sedia ada ini membolehkan penggunaan biodiesel diperluas tanpa memerlukan pembangunan keseluruhan infrastruktur baharu, sekali gus menyokong aspirasi Pelan Hala Tuju Peralihan Tenaga Negara (NETR) dan Dasar Agrikomoditi Negara 2030 (DAKN 2030).

Keberkesanan awal program itu dapat dilihat apabila Menteri Perladangan dan Komoditi Noraini Ahmad memaklumkan di Dewan Rakyat pada Oktober bahawa pelaksanaan B15 menjimatkan purata 23.62 juta liter diesel petroleum sebulan bagi tempoh Jun hingga Ogos.

Walaupun penjimatan itu tidak semestinya menurunkan harga diesel di pasaran, ia menunjukkan kemampuan sumber tempatan mengurangkan penggunaan bahan api fosil yang terdedah kepada ketidaktentuan global.

Ketua Kompleks Biorefineri Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) Hidayah Ariffin sebelum ini menjelaskan peningkatan penggunaan biodiesel mampu memanjangkan daya tahan bekalan diesel domestik ketika krisis tenaga.
Pandangan itu mengukuhkan kepentingan biodiesel sebagai sebahagian daripada usaha kerajaan mempelbagaikan sumber tenaga, khususnya ketika pasaran petroleum antarabangsa sukar dijangka.
Manfaat kepada pertanian dan perladangan

Selain sektor pengangkutan, penggunaan biodiesel berpotensi memberi manfaat kepada pertanian dan perladangan yang bergantung kepada diesel untuk menggerakkan jentera, mengepam air serta mengangkut hasil pengeluaran.

Bekalan bahan api yang lebih terjamin dapat membantu pengusaha merancang operasi dan mengurangkan risiko kenaikan kos mendadak. Perkara ini penting terutama kepada petani dan pekebun kecil yang mempunyai ruang kewangan terhad untuk menampung perbelanjaan tambahan.

Bagaimanapun, mandat B15 ketika ini tertumpu kepada sektor pengangkutan. Kerajaan perlu meneliti kesesuaiannya untuk jentera pertanian dan perladangan, termasuk kemampuan enjin, kemudahan bekalan serta kos penggunaan.
Tanpa persediaan tersebut, manfaat diharapkan mungkin tidak sampai kepada golongan yang paling memerlukannya.
Pada masa sama, peluasan biodiesel turut menyediakan pasaran domestik lebih besar kepada industri sawit negara.

Menurut KPK, pelaksanaan B15 dianggarkan meningkatkan keperluan minyak sawit mentah sekitar 330,000 tan setahun. Dengan mengambil kira pelaksanaannya bermula Jun, penggunaan minyak sawit bagi Program Biodiesel Negara diunjurkan mencecah kira-kira 1.13 juta tan menjelang akhir 2026.
Permintaan tambahan ini berpotensi membantu industri sawit, termasuk pekebun kecil, serta menggalakkan pelaburan dalam teknologi pemprosesan bahan api alternatif.

Pensyarah kanan Ahmad Muhaimin Roslan daripada UPM turut melihat pelaksanaan B15 sebagai peluang mengukuhkan industri sawit dan membangunkan teknologi hijau, selain meningkatkan keselamatan tenaga negara.

Namun, peningkatan permintaan minyak sawit untuk biodiesel perlu diimbangi dengan keperluan industri makanan dan pasaran eksport supaya tidak menimbulkan tekanan baharu terhadap bekalan serta harga bahan mentah.
Peralihan tenaga perlu realistik

Dari sudut alam sekitar, biodiesel mempunyai kelebihan kerana dihasilkan daripada sumber boleh diperbaharui dan lebih mudah terurai secara biologi. Penggunaannya juga berpotensi mengurangkan pelepasan bahan pencemar tertentu, bergantung kepada jenis enjin dan kadar campuran.

Bagaimanapun, biodiesel bukan bahan api bebas karbon. Kesan keseluruhan terhadap alam sekitar masih bergantung kepada kaedah penanaman sawit, pemprosesan bahan mentah dan penggunaan tenaga sepanjang rantaian pengeluaran.

Pensyarah kanan Fakulti Pengurusan dan Perniagaan Universiti Teknologi Mara Chong Siew Huay sebelum ini turut berpandangan biodiesel langkah peralihan praktikal ke arah tenaga lebih bersih, tetapi bukan penyelesaian tunggal untuk jangka panjang.
Justeru, kerajaan wajar mempergiat penyelidikan terhadap bahan mentah alternatif seperti minyak masak terpakai dan sisa sawit bagi mengurangkan kebergantungan kepada satu sumber.

Pendekatan ini selaras sasaran Malaysia mencapai pelepasan karbon sifar bersih menjelang 2050, selain menyokong Matlamat Pembangunan Mampan (SDG) berkaitan tenaga bersih, pertumbuhan ekonomi dan penggunaan sumber secara bertanggungjawab.

Namun, komitmen terhadap pembangunan ekonomi hijau perlu disertai hasil yang boleh diukur. Data mengenai penjimatan diesel, kos pengeluaran biodiesel dan kesannya kepada pengguna wajar diumumkan secara berkala bagi memastikan pelaksanaan program kekal berkesan.

Malaysia mempunyai kelebihan sumber sawit, teknologi dan kemudahan untuk membangunkan industri biodiesel secara lebih meluas. Apa yang diperlukan ialah pelaksanaan berperingkat dengan mengambil kira kemampuan industri serta kepentingan pengguna.

B15 boleh menjadi langkah penting dalam menghadapi ketidaktentuan tenaga dunia, tetapi kejayaan akhirnya bergantung kepada sejauh mana dasar ini mampu menjamin bekalan, mengekang tekanan kos dan memberi manfaat nyata kepada ekonomi negara.
Penulis ialah pengarang Meja Berita Bahasa Melayu FMT.

849e6bdce637a08e: SUNDERLAND, Nov 9 — Sunderland hauled themselves off the bottom of the Premier League as Enzo Le Fee’s penalty earned a huge 1-0 win over Chelsea for embattled boss Regis Le Bris.
The Frenchman was under pressure after a dismal 2-0 home defeat to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League on Thursday put his position in doubt ahead of an international break.
Sunderland, though, bounced back for a huge three points thanks to two controversial penalty decisions.
Chelsea were furious that Cole Palmer was not awarded a spot-kick for a foul by Luke O’Nien moments before the only goal of the game.
A VAR review deemed the contact made was outside the area and therefore could not be overturned.
Sunderland were awarded a penalty at the other end 10 minutes before half-time.
The visitors were again aggrieved that Levi Colwill was adjudged to have fouled Brian Brobbey as both players grappled in their attempt to reach the ball.
Le Fee dispatched the resulting spot-kick past Mike Penders and Sunderland held on for just a second league win of the season.
Speaking about both incidents, Alonso said: “I haven’t seen Cole’s one, but I’ve been told that there was a chance that it would be a fair penalty and it could have been given.
“The other one, not happy with how we defended that situation, something that we could avoid. From that action to give a penalty is not good from us.”
Chelsea missed the presence of Joao Pedro up front as Palmer and Morgan Rogers were kept in check by the home side.
A fourth defeat in 10 league games under Xabi Alonso leaves the Blues in fifth, two points outside the top four.
“I think we didn’t deserve more than probably one point, the game was really close,” Alonso said.
“We were against the low block, we missed a bit of patience, a bit of quality, creativity in the last third to create more chances.
“We need to be more consistent to move the ball from one side to the other, we didn’t do good enough.” — AFP
92bb8d3f047f3be3: ALOR GAJAH, Nov 9 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is stepping up efforts to win over young voters, particularly first-time voters, through more targeted campaigning, including the use of social media and face-to-face engagement, in the 16th Melaka state election.

1568a4b59aca9534: MANCHESTER, Nov 9 — Manchester United twice came from two goals down to salvage a remarkable 4-4 draw against Aston Villa yesterday and potentially save manager Michael Carrick’s job.
Goals in stoppage time from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescued a point, but United will spend a two-week international break in the relegation zone.
Carrick’s team conceded twice inside the opening four minutes as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson punished errors from goalkeeper Senne Lammens.
The Red Devils rallied to level at half-time thanks to a Bruno Fernandes penalty and Youri Tielemans’s first goal since moving to Old Trafford from Villa.
A thrilling fightback from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday gave Carrick a lifeline.
This time the comeback fell short as more woeful defending handed Villa two more goals inside the first eight minutes of the second period.
John McGinn converted from the spot after Diogo Dalot upended Alysson before Leon Goretzka bundled in from close range.
Yet, there was a final twist in the tale as Zirkzee steered home before Dorgu pounced when Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki failed to connect with a corner in the 96th minute.
‘We want new owners’
Carrick was handed a stay of execution after a 3-0 home drubbing by Bournemouth a fortnight ago.
However, he faces an anxious wait to see if the United board install a replacement before a daunting trip to Liverpool on November 22.
“We haven’t won enough games, but I expect to move forward and keep working on the things that we’ve been working on,” Carrick told Sky Sports.
Former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Bayern Munich and Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann are among the leading contenders to take charge if Carrick is dismissed.
Saturday’s results saw United slip into the relegation zone after August for the first time in 40 years.
A draw keeps them in the bottom three with just eight points from 10 games.
For the first time in Premier League history they found themselves 2-0 down inside four minutes, in large part due to goalkeeper Lammens.
The Belgian allowed Alysson’s strike to slip between his legs with just one minute on the clock.
From another tame Alysson effort less than three minutes later, Lammens could only parry and present Nicolas Jackson with a gift for his sixth goal in his last six league games.
The United fans had again turned their ire towards the club’s owners pre-match.
A banner read: “We don’t want a new stadium, we want new owners,” as protests towards a move away from Old Trafford gather steam.
That anger was directed towards the players in cries of “you’re not fit to wear the shirt” in the wake of the second Villa goal.
Yet, the shock of going behind summoned a response as United again found their feet at 2-0 down.
Just as against Roma, the fightback was started by Matheus Cunha winning a penalty, converted by Fernandes.
United built momentum before levelling just before the break when Tielemans drilled low beyond Suzuki.
What should have been the launching pad for another stirring fightback quickly fell flat at the start of the second half.
Dalot dived in foolishly to trip Alysson and McGinn made amends for missing from the spot in last weekend’s 1-1 draw against Fulham.
Moments later Leny Yoro headed a McGinn free-kick off his own crossbar and Goretzka forced the ball over the line in the goalmouth scramble that ensued.
The closing stages were played out to the tune of more protests against United’s unpopular American owners, the Glazer family, until the home side hauled themselves off the canvas again.
Zirkzee’s cool finish reawakened the crowd and left Villa clinging on.
Much to the frustration of Unai Emery, his side could not resist the late assault as Suzuki flapped at Fernandes’s corner and Dorgu accepted the gift.
“I am disappointed but we move on.” said Emery. “It is very important to analyse (the game) deeply.” — AFP
2c36dc3beb40f1f0: SYDNEY: Marnus Labuschagne was axed from Australia's squad today for their upcoming four-Test series against New Zealand, paying the price for a long run of poor form.
The number three, who has played 68 Tests, was under-pressure going into their recent tour of South Africa and failed to fire across the three Tests.
"At this stage we won't be considering Marn for selection for certainly that first Test, but for the New Zealand series," chairman of selectors George Bailey told cricket.com.au.
"There's been a lot of speculation around his place in the team.
"So I think this gives him a little bit of space and clears up a bit of conjecture as we work through the next round of (Sheffield) Shield cricket."
Labuschagne, who at one stage was the world's top-ranked batter, had a tortured tour of South Africa, where his highest score was 39.
The 32-year-old has not scored a century since the 2023 Ashes series against England, but Bailey left the door open for a recall if he again finds form in the domestic red-ball competition.
"And I think we all know how good and how effective Marnus can be at his best. But that performance hasn't been there.

471e5c32464da7fa: WASHINGTON, Nov 9 — US President Donald Trump yesterday cast doubt on renewed fighting with Iran, telling CNN that it was “highly unlikely” so long as talks progressed.
In recent weeks, Trump has threatened to renew strikes with US media reports suggesting that hostilities could resume after the US midterm elections this week.

“The answer is highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary… I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don’t know how hard I hit them,” Trump said, while warning that any decision to resume hostilities “depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement.”
Trump previously acknowledged that the highly unpopular war with Iran was at least partially responsible for the stinging defeat that his Republican Party suffered in Tuesday’s vote.
In the CNN interview Sunday, Trump once again suggested that the economic pressure Iran is under will force its leaders into accepting a peace deal on the United States’ terms.
“They’re a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301 percent inflation,” Trump claimed. “They’re withering away financially. We’ve hit them militarily. We could finish them off.”
But earlier on Sunday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi suggested peace talks had been paused while the political fallout of the Democratic Party’s landslide victory was being assessed.

“For the past few days, there has been no more travel (by mediators), and the reason for this is the shock that the election results in the United States have caused to everyone,” Araghchi told state television. “We now have to see how long it will take for them to digest these results, in order to determine how we are going to move forward.”

Iran continues to at least partly block traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which has dented oil supplies out of the Gulf. That, in turn, has driven up gasoline prices in the United States, contributing to the unpopularity of the war. — AFP

Charles, 77, in military uniform as commander-in-chief of Britain’s armed forces, was accompanied by his elder son and heir, Prince William, 44, as well as other senior members of the royal family.
Queen Camilla, 79, and William’s wife, Princess Catherine, 44, watched proceedings from a balcony of the nearby foreign ministry.

b5de7cdc64f321ec: WASHINGTON, Nov 9 — Japan’s Godzilla Minus Zero roared to first place in the North American box office over the weekend, industry estimates showed yesterday, gobbling up US$31.6 million (RM128.1 million) in sales on its opening weekend.
Set in 1949 as postwar Japan looks to rebuild, the film sees a new threat emerge: a giant three-headed dragon-like monster called King Ghidorah.
Enter Godzilla — believed defeated in the 2023 Godzilla Minus One, but radioactively regenerated — who takes on the three-headed beast with at least some human assistance.
“This weekend’s opening takes the Japanese production to a new level — it’s nearly three times the previous opening in December 2023,” veteran industry analyst David A. Gross wrote.
Godzilla in this making is the same iconic beast that many North American viewers know from the 1998 Sony Pictures film, but he exists in a different storyline with different producers.
Directed by Takashi Yamazaki, Godzilla Minus Zero is produced by Japan’s Toho and distributed in North America by GKIDS.
In second place sat a far-less scary beast: The Cat in the Hat.
The legendary Dr Seuss feline brought in an estimated US$20.5 million in its opening weekend in the latest instalment distributed by Warner Bros.
Gross warned that Dr Seuss films don’t typically perform well outside the United States, but may be able to make up for that by earning money on streaming platforms or through television rights.
Marching into third place was Angel Studio’s Drummer Boy, which banged out US$9.3 million at the box office, according to estimates by Exhibitor Relations Co.

The unique film — a combination of historical drama and musical — follows an American soldier and his brother during the Revolutionary war, with the brother marrying an enslaved woman and fighting for the British.
Gross said the film brought in double what would be expected of a similar film on its opening weekend.
“Angel specialises in inspirational stories and they know how to reach this audience,” Gross wrote in his weekly newsletter.
Fourth place went to A24’s You Can See Everything, the biopic that follows convicted fraudster Elizabeth Holmes in the month before she began an 11-year prison sentence.
The film brought in about US$8.9 million over the weekend, bringing its four-week total to an estimated US$79.8 million.

Gross noted that it was “one of only five Indian wide releases in the US” over the last three decades.
Rounding out the top 10:

7f152ca6be50c785: From Moaz Nair

For generations, higher education functioned as a cornerstone of the Malaysian social contract. A tertiary degree, achieved through rigorous academic adherence, effectively guaranteed upward socioeconomic mobility and entry into the professional middle class.
Today, however, structural shifts induced by advanced automation and artificial intelligence have fundamentally fractured this predictable linear trajectory.

While aggregate macroeconomic indicators present a resilient domestic economy, micro-level data from the labour market reveals a systemic disruption. The proliferation of generative AI tools has effectively dismantled the entry-level tier of corporate employment, placing the return on investment of a traditional university degree under severe scrutiny.
Are educators in our higher educational institutions prepared to embrace this technology?

Data from the statistics department illustrates the depth of this structural paradox. While the national unemployment rate stands at a remarkably healthy 2.9%, youth unemployment (ages 15 to 24) remains stubbornly elevated at 10.1%, representing approximately 291,300 young citizens experiencing market-entry barriers.
Of more concern is the pervasive rise of skills-related underemployment.

According to the latest graduate statistics, 32.2% of the employed graduate workforce, or 1.6 million people occupy roles categorised as semi-skilled or low-skilled. The visual narrative of tertiary-educated youth operating within the gig economy or basic service sectors rather than corporate offices is no longer an anomaly; it is an empirical trend.
Young people who would normally have gone into routine professional jobs are now serving customers in tea shops. This is not what our youth aspire to.

Historically, entry-level positions served a dual purpose: they fulfilled corporate administrative needs while acting as a vital practical apprenticeship for fresh graduates. Tasks such as data compilation, minute-taking, draft formulation, and presentation synthesis allowed new entrants to internalise corporate culture, systemic hierarchies, and operational soft skills.

With AI software now executing these routine, algorithmic tasks at a fraction of the temporal and financial cost, private firms are actively reducing their junior headcounts and altering hiring thresholds.

Emerging market analysis suggests that up to 40% of standard roles historically allocated to fresh graduates have undergone severe contractions due to routine automation. Consequently, universities face an immediate existential mandate.
Institutions can no longer function as passive, credential-issuing entities, or they risk producing graduates equipped only with obsolete paper qualifications.

To prevent a structural underemployment crisis from solidifying into permanent socioeconomic inequality, a comprehensive paradigm shift must occur across institutional curricula. The traditional instructional methodology predicated on stagnant, rote-learning lectures and memory-based assessments is fundamentally incompatible with an economy wherein raw information retrieval is instant and costless.

Higher education institutions must intentionally pivot towards developing capabilities that lie beyond the current frontier of machine learning. This requires an academic focus on high-order cognitive processes, including multi-system thinking, advanced cross-disciplinary innovation, ethical governance, and sophisticated emotional intelligence.

Recognising the urgency of this transition, the higher education ministry has proactively initiated key systemic changes, recently undertaking a comprehensive review of 455 public university study programmes.

The ministry has set an aggressive target to integrate foundational AI components into 80% of all public undergraduate courses, alongside the ongoing expansion of specialised entities like the Faculty of Artificial Intelligence at Universiti Teknologi Malaysia.
The broader national blueprint aims to generate 30,000 highly skilled AI graduates by 2030 to mitigate the effects of rapid workspace automation.

However, transforming formal degree structures is merely one component of a holistic strategy. A real-world equilibrium requires immediate, coordinated fiscal and policy interventions executed in tandem with industry demands. To successfully navigate this transition, public and private stakeholders must scale up initiatives across three essential pillars.

First, academic faculties must build institutionalised, dynamic bridges with corporate partners. This collaboration ensures that university modules adjust symmetrically alongside rapidly evolving technological frontiers, shifting student assessment metrics toward practical problem-solving.

Second, leveraging national frameworks like the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 and substantial public sector technology allocations, universities must aggressively channel funds into high-performance computing infrastructure, advanced hardware acquisition, and research commercialisation funds.

Finally, stakeholders must expand lifelong reskilling ecosystems. This means scaling up structural upskilling pipelines such as micro-credentials and technical courses certified by agencies like TalentCorp or funded through HRD Corp to swiftly transition underemployed or displaced workers into high-growth, non-routine fields like semiconductor IC design, cybersecurity, and digital health.

The proliferation of artificial intelligence software does not inherently dictate the obsolescence of the university system; rather, it demands its radical re-engineering. If higher education institutions fail to adapt, the domestic economy risks widening its structural inequalities, trapping a large segment of the domestic talent pool in low-value service roles while a thin, technologically elite class captures the premium of digital growth.

Higher education must act with proactive foresight and structural courage. By transforming the curriculum from a static knowledge repository into a dynamic incubator for uniquely human innovation, Malaysian universities can ensure that their graduates remain the primary architects of the national digital economy.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
5fe45eaf09e0f584: KUALA LUMPUR: At Batu Caves in Selangor, the colours were enough to stop Evelina Nesterenko in her tracks.

The 24-year-old Russian tourist, visiting the landmark for the first time, found herself drawn into the sights and atmosphere of Deepavali at the Sri Subramaniar Swamy Temple, where devotees and visitors filled the grounds with vibrant hues and movement yesterday.
“It’s really impressive. It’s so beautiful and colourful - I just want to go and look at everything and see them with my own eyes,” said Nesterenko, an English teacher based in Vietnam.
Her trip to Malaysia was partly inspired by friends who had spoken warmly of the country, but she was also curious about its cultural diversity.

“Russia is also very multinational and we have lots of festivals for different cultures,” she told Bernama. “So, it’s really nice that there is a place for everyone and that people are interested in different national festivals.”

German tourist Lena Koetter was struck by something slightly different: the atmosphere of people simply enjoying the occasion together. After two weeks in Malaysia, she said the warmth she experienced from locals was one of the highlights of her visit.
“I really like the people here. They are so kind,” she said, adding that the celebrations, complete with fireworks, offered a welcome sense of joy and togetherness.

For Bhanuprakash, a bank officer from India who has lived in Malaysia for nearly a year, Batu Caves felt both familiar and different. The prayers and rituals reminded him of Deepavali celebrations back home, but Malaysia’s open-house tradition was new to him.
“Normally, Diwali for us involves celebrating at our place. Not open house, we don't go to parties; but at our own place, with our own family," he explained.

In Gua Musang, Kelantan, the mood was more intimate. At the Sri Subramanyaswamy Temple, built at the foot of a limestone hill, devotees gathered not only from the surrounding area but also from Selangor, Johor and overseas.
Temple secretary N Darnam said its location was part of its charm, with the limestone backdrop giving the celebrations a setting quite unlike the bustle of Batu Caves.
More than 100 visitors attended this year, including devotees from Nepal, India and Bangladesh, as well as foreign workers employed in plantations around the district.
For devotee P Jegan, the trip carried a more personal meaning. The 37-year-old works in Kajang but returned to his hometown two days early to continue a tradition started by his late father.

“Every year, I return to Gua Musang to celebrate Deepavali with my family at this temple," he told Bernama yesterday. "This has been practised by my late father for a long time, and I want to continue it.”
Today, he will be celebrating with his wife's family in Kota Bharu.

For T Shahtishwaran, 28, an early-morning visit to the temple was also an opportunity to reconnect with relatives, friends, and the wider Indian community before continuing the day with visits to family homes.
From one of Malaysia’s most recognisable Hindu landmarks to a smaller temple tucked beneath a limestone hill, the settings could hardly be more different.
Yet in both places, Deepavali offers much the same thing: a reason to gather, to return, to look around with fresh eyes - and, for some, to feel at home.
07264201d8238518: Bagi generasi terdahulu, sistem pendidikan tinggi berfungsi sebagai asas kepada kontrak sosial Malaysia. Segulung ijazah yang diperoleh melalui usaha akademik yang gigih hampir pasti menjamin peningkatan taraf sosioekonomi dan kemasukan ke dalam golongan kelas menengah profesional. Namun, hari ini perubahan struktur yang dibawa oleh automasi canggih dan kecerdasan buatan (AI) telah memecahkan corak masa depan yang mudah dijangka ini.

Walaupun petunjuk makroekonomi keseluruhan menunjukkan ekonomi negara yang berdaya tahan, data mikro daripada pasaran buruh mendedahkan gangguan yang ketara. Perkembangan alat AI generatif telah menjejaskan peluang pekerjaan peringkat permulaan di sektor korporat. Situasi ini membuatkan pulangan pelaburan untuk segulung ijazah universiti tradisional kini dipersoal. Persoalannya, adakah para pendidik di institusi pengajian tinggi tempatan kita bersedia untuk menerima teknologi ini?

Data daripada Jabatan Perangkaan Malaysia (DOSM) menunjukkan betapa seriusnya percanggahan struktur ini. Walaupun kadar pengangguran negara berada pada tahap yang sangat baik iaitu 2.9%, kadar pengangguran belia (berumur 15 hingga 24 tahun) tetap tinggi pada paras 10.1%. Ini mewakili kira-kira 291,300 rakyat muda yang menghadapi kesukaran untuk memasuki pasaran kerja.

Apa yang lebih membimbangkan berbanding pengangguran mutlak adalah peningkatan isu guna tenaga tidak penuh (underemployment) yang berkaitan dengan kemahiran. Menurut Statistik Siswazah terkini daripada DOSM, sebanyak 32.2% daripada tenaga kerja siswazah yang bekerja—bersamaan dengan 1.6 juta individu—bekerja dalam peranan yang dikategorikan sebagai separuh mahir atau kurang mahir. Senario anak muda berkelulusan tinggi bekerja dalam ekonomi gig atau sektor perkhidmatan asas berbanding di pejabat korporat bukan lagi satu perkara ganjil, sebaliknya ia sudah menjadi satu trend yang nyata. Kita melihat anak muda yang sepatutnya mengisi jawatan profesional rutin, kini bekerja melayan pelanggan di kedai teh. Ini bukanlah apa yang dicita-citakan oleh belia kita.

Dari segi sejarah, jawatan peringkat permulaan mempunyai dua fungsi utama: ia memenuhi keperluan pentadbiran syarikat sambil menjadi tempat latihan praktikal yang penting untuk graduan baharu. Tugasan seperti menyusun data, mencatat minit mesyuarat, menyediakan draf, dan menghasilkan pembentangan membolehkan pekerja baharu memahami budaya korporat, sistem hierarki, dan kemahiran insaniah (soft skills). Oleh kerana aplikasi AI kini boleh melakukan tugasan rutin ini dengan kos masa dan kewangan yang jauh lebih murah, syarikat swasta kini mengurangkan pengambilan pekerja junior dan mengubah syarat pengambilan pekerja mereka.

Analisis pasaran semasa menunjukkan bahawa sehingga 40% daripada jawatan biasa yang dahulunya diisi oleh graduan baharu telah berkurangan dengan mendadak akibat automasi rutin. Kesannya, universiti kini menghadapi cabaran besar yang perlu ditangani segera. Institusi pendidikan tidak boleh lagi berfungsi sekadar sebagai tempat mengeluarkan sijil, atau mereka berisiko melahirkan graduan yang hanya dilengkapi dengan kelayakan kertas yang sudah lapuk.

Bagi mengelakkan krisis guna tenaga tidak penuh ini daripada menjadi ketidaksamaan sosioekonomi yang kekal, perubahan kaedah yang menyeluruh mesti dilakukan pada kurikulum institusi. Kaedah pengajaran tradisional—yang bergantung kepada kuliah hafalan yang statik dan peperiksaan berasaskan ingatan—sudah tidak sesuai lagi dengan sistem ekonomi masa kini, di mana maklumat mentah boleh diperoleh dengan serta-merta tanpa sebarang kos.

Institusi pengajian tinggi mesti beralih secara terancang ke arah membina keupayaan yang tidak boleh dilakukan oleh mesin. Ini memerlukan fokus akademik terhadap proses pemikiran tahap tinggi, termasuk pemikiran pelbagai sistem, inovasi merentas disiplin yang maju, tadbir urus beretika, dan kecerdasan emosi (EQ) yang tinggi.

Menyedari kepentingan peralihan ini, Kementerian Pendidikan Tinggi (KPT) telah mula mengambil langkah proaktif dengan menyemak semula 455 program pengajian di universiti awam. KPT telah menetapkan sasaran utama untuk menyerapkan elemen asas AI ke dalam 80% daripada semua kursus ijazah sarjana muda awam. Langkah ini berjalan seiring dengan usaha memperluas entiti khusus seperti Fakulti Kecerdasan Buatan di Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM). Pelan tindakan nasional yang lebih luas menyasarkan untuk melahirkan 30,000 graduan AI berkemahiran tinggi menjelang tahun 2030 bagi mengurangkan kesan automasi di tempat kerja yang berlaku dengan pantas.

Bagaimanapun, mengubah struktur ijazah formal hanyalah sebahagian daripada strategi yang menyeluruh. Keseimbangan dalam dunia sebenar memerlukan tindakan kewangan dan dasar yang diselaraskan segera bersama dengan keperluan industri. Untuk menjayakan peralihan ini, pihak awam dan swasta mesti mempertingkatkan usaha melalui tiga tonggak utama:

Pertama, fakulti akademik mesti membina hubungan yang dinamik dengan rakan korporat. Kerjasama ini penting bagi memastikan modul universiti sentiasa berubah mengikut perkembangan teknologi, sekali gus mengalih penilaian pelajar ke arah penyelesaian masalah secara praktikal.

Kedua, dengan memanfaatkan pelan negara seperti Pelan Induk Perindustrian Baharu (NIMP) 2030 serta peruntukan teknologi sektor awam, universiti mesti menyalurkan dana secara agresif ke dalam infrastruktur pengkomputeran berprestasi tinggi, pembelian perkakasan canggih, dan dana pengkomersialan penyelidikan.

Akhir sekali, pihak berkepentingan mesti memperluas ekosistem pembelajaran sepanjang hayat. Ini bermakna memperbanyakkan program peningkatan kemahiran—seperti mikro-kredential dan kursus teknikal yang diiktiraf oleh agensi seperti TalentCorp atau dibiayai melalui HRD Corp. Langkah ini penting untuk membantu pekerja yang kurang mendapat peluang atau yang kehilangan pekerjaan beralih dengan cepat ke bidang baharu yang berkembang pesat dan bukan bersifat rutin, seperti reka bentuk litar bersepadu (IC) semikonduktor, keselamatan siber, dan kesihatan digital.

Perkembangan AI yang pesat tidak bermakna sistem universiti akan terus luput; sebaliknya, ia menuntut perubahan struktur yang radikal. Jika institusi pengajian tinggi gagal menyesuaikan diri, ekonomi negara berisiko menghadapi jurang ketidaksamaan struktur yang lebih besar. Keadaan ini akan memerangkap sebahagian besar bakat tempatan dalam sektor perkhidmatan bernilai rendah, manakala golongan elit teknologi yang kecil pula akan menguasai sepenuhnya hasil pertumbuhan digital.

Sektor pendidikan tinggi mesti bertindak dengan pandangan jauh dan berani melakukan perubahan. Dengan mengubah kurikulum daripada sebuah tempat menyimpan ilmu yang statik kepada pusat inovasi manusia yang dinamik, universiti di Malaysia dapat memastikan graduan mereka kekal menjadi penggerak utama kepada ekonomi digital negara.

338fd982ef5c709a: Reigning Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova defeated Marta Kostyuk 6-2, 6-4 on Sunday in the opening match of the season-ending WTA Finals at Indian Wells.

275c334d073f8493: BUENOS AIRES: Pope Leo XIV delivered a stinging critique of President Javier Milei's harsh austerity measures Sunday, insisting growth must benefit all in a speech met with rapturous applause.
"The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy," he said, shortly after landing in Argentina on the second leg of a Latin America tour.
Leo stressed the plight of those who, "despite hard work, nonetheless struggle to meet their household's needs."

He spoke out in defence of the poor and pensioners, insisting that "particular concern be shown for those affected by illness, dependency and disability" - a veiled reference to the government's controversial cuts to disability assistance.
And he told Milei, known for his foul-mouthed diatribes, that strengthening democracy required a "willingness to listen" and the "careful use of words."
Milei, for his part, said his government was working to avoid "punishing the Argentines of tomorrow in order to benefit the Argentines of today."
Appeals for unity
The visit is the first by a pontiff to Argentina in nearly four decades, and Leo was met with calls to help mend deep divisions in the country after three years of austerity under Milei.
Leo arrived in Buenos Aires from Uruguay, where he began his first trip as pope to Latin America, the world's most Catholic continent which is becoming increasingly secular.
Argentina is the home country of the late pope, Francis.
Milei famously insulted Francis for his pro-poor teachings. Leo said he was "retracing" Francis's steps.
'Unite us'
Argentines are hoping the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics will help unite the country, which is bitterly divided between supporters and opponents of Milei.

"Just like the World Cup unites us, hopefully the pope will too," said Liliana Deblauwe, a 68-year-old retired teacher who waited with hundreds of people to see the pope visit a monument to liberation hero Jose de San Martin.
Hundreds more chanting "Papa Leon" (Spanish for Leo) gathered outside the presidential palace, where he was hosted by Milei.
Brian Inacio Rodriguez, a 26-year-old job seeker, spent five days traveling overland from Ushuaia, at the very tip of South America, to see the pontiff.
He said he hoped he brought "much peace to Argentina."
Just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer, Pope Leo is on an ambitious 12-day tour of the continent where he served nearly two decades as a missionary.
In Uruguay, he condemned drug violence and urged an end to child poverty.
In Buenos Aires, he insisted on the importance of "personal integrity" in public office, stressing that "corruption undermines the confidence of citizens in their institutions."
The Argentine stage of his visit aims to boost the flagging faith of a country left disappointed by Francis's failure to visit during his papacy.
It will also act as a litmus test of support for the Church.
Some 57.7% of people identified as Catholic in a recent University of Buenos Aires poll, down from around 90 percent in the 1960s.
Leo will visit a home for disabled people and a prison and celebrate three open-air masses.
The Church has said it expects a total of seven million faithful at the various events.
'Imbecile' Francis

Milei came to office on a promise to revive Argentina's ailing economy and tame runaway inflation by shrinking the welfare state, targeting public hospitals, universities and pensioners in particular.
The poverty rate has swung wildly since he came to power - increasing to 32.3% in September.
A close ally of US president Donald Trump, with a similar combative style, Milei had a tense relationship with Francis.
On the campaign trail the cost-cutting economist called his countryman an "imbecile" for championing social justice.
Once in office, however, he softened his tone, but he continues to heap insults on the press and opposition.
His relationship with Leo has so far been cordial, but the local Catholic Church has heavily criticized him for treating key social services solely as a budgetary constraint.
Milei has also been criticised for restricting several democratic freedoms, including the right to protest. But he maintains a loyal supporter base for drastically reducing inflation.

0dbb880f23879fa2: PARIS: In a rematch of their memorable US Open quarterfinal match, Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz defeated Ben Shelton 7-6 (5), 7-5 on Sunday to win his ninth ATP Masters 1000 title and first at the Rolex Paris Masters.
Shelton bested Alcaraz in September in a memorable five-set quarterfinal marathon at the US Open.
The US Open was Alcaraz's first tournament in four months because of a wrist injury.
Since then, he has won in Tokyo, Vienna and now Paris. He is 4-1 vs. Shelton in the Lexus ATP Head2Head series.
"It is something I have been chasing for a long time," Alcaraz said after the match.
"Some of the toughest defeats I ever had in my career I have had here. Finally, I got my level here. I found the right path and the right way to do things.
"I am really proud of myself and the team. The way they have pushed me forward. This one means a lot to me."
Alcaraz, 23, rallied from 0-40 and down 2-1 to hold serve in the first set.
Shelton then saved two break points to stay on serve, but Alcaraz overpowered Shelton in the tiebreak.
Shelton had Alcaraz a break down in the second set, but the Spaniard hit several forehand winners to come back. He sealed the win in the 1-hour, 57-minute match on his second match point.
"Today was one of the toughest challenges we have in tennis, facing Ben Shelton," Alcaraz said.
"He is a great player, person, champion and he is doing better and better every tournament. I am just really happy I found a way.
"Putting his serves into play and trying to be myself on court. I am really happy I finally got it and this one is going to be really special."

Alcaraz, who now has wins in seven of the nine Masters 1000 tournaments, joined Novak Djokovic and Rafael Nadal as the only players in series history (since 1990) to win Masters 1000 events in five straight years.

728a17e13814fa00: KUALA LUMPUR: Attorney-general Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar yesterday questioned the diligence exercised in preparing official judicial documents for the implementation of Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest order.

Commenting on the Kuala Lumpur High Court's Order of Discharge relating to the former prime minister's sentence, which has raised questions among legal practitioners, he said such issues should not have arisen had the parties involved scrutinised every detail.
Dusuki said the defects identified in the document were glaring and should not have occurred.
"This should not have happened if the parties concerned had been careful. The mistake is glaring and has caused unnecessary problems," he said.
The defects in question relate particularly to the accuracy of the terminology and legal provisions used in the document.

The document was issued by the High Court after the RM50 million fine imposed on the former Pekan member of parliament, as a condition for serving the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest, was paid using funds collected through the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund launched by Umno.

However, the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) moved to temporarily suspend the implementation of Najib's house arrest to allow the prosecution to seek further clarification on the actual interpretation of the Conditional Pardon Order granted by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
The A-GC's decision drew criticism from Istana Negara, which said any arguments disputing the conditional pardon granted to Najib could amount to defying the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's decree.
Istana Negara stressed that all conditions stipulated in the conditional pardon order had been fulfilled and that its implementation should not give rise to prolonged confusion or uncertainty.
It also maintained that the pardon order was clear, explicit and unambiguous, and had no bearing on any other cases involving Najib.
On the audience with Sultan Ibrahim, Dusuki declined to comment further.
However, it is understood that the audience could take place tomorrow.

On Sept 18, Najib, 73, who is a former Umno president, received a conditional pardon from the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.

He was sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million after being found guilty by the Kuala Lumpur High Court on July 28, 2020, on seven charges relating to the misappropriation of RM42 million from SRC International.
On Aug 23, 2022, the Federal Court dismissed Najib's final appeal and upheld his conviction and sentence. He began serving his prison term at Kajang Prison on the same day.
He subsequently submitted a pardon petition to the king on Sept 2, 2022. The application was considered at a Pardons Board meeting on Jan 29, 2024.

On Feb 2, 2024, the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department announced the Pardons Board's decision to reduce Najib's prison sentence from 12 years to six years, while the fine was reduced from RM210 million to RM50 million.

0edd161ce38b4308: PETALING JAYA: For Usha Suppiah, Deepavali has always been about family. It meant a house filled with relatives, festive cooking and children gathered around to make murukku.
This year, however, the festival will be marked by the absence of her eldest son, K Indiran.
On Feb 18, the 22-year-old armed forces trooper was found unconscious at the 10th Mile Army Camp in Kuantan. He died two days later while receiving treatment.
“The last time Indiran was here, we were all happy. But this year, he’s not around, and when we feel one of the family members is not around, we feel 'one kind',” Usha, 52, told FMT Lifestyle.
“I really miss him. All of the family members miss him. But still life must go on.”

Following Hindu tradition, they will not be celebrating Deepavali for a year after the death of a family member. Still, Usha and her three other children will observe prayers and have a modest gathering with relatives travelling from different parts of the country.

Her youngest daughter, 12, has been trying to understand why the celebrations will be different this year. “She asked, ‘Amma, why is Anna (big brother) not around? We cannot celebrate Deepavali, right?’
“I said to her, ‘Yes, Anna is not around, but we are still doing prayers. We are not celebrating in a grand way, but still we are doing makan-makan'," Usha, a nurse, said.

In previous years, Indiran would return home about a week before Deepavali to help clean and decorate the house, accompany his mother on shopping trips, and prepare traditional treats such as murukku.
He was also the life of family gatherings, often entertaining his relatives and friends.
“Indiran’s uncles and friends would gather, have drinks, and then Indiran would dance and sing. We would all fully enjoy ourselves because he would dance with us. That, I cannot forget," Usha said.

Indiran had also taken on greater responsibilities at home after his father, a Royal Malaysian Air Force officer, died in an aircraft crash in 2016. As the oldest of four children, he stepped up to help his mother and look after his siblings.
“He took care of his sisters and brother. He would cook rice, clean the house ... just like my husband, he would help out with all the housework.”

Given that her husband had died in an aircraft crash, Usha was initially reluctant to let Indiran join the armed forces. Eventually, however, she accepted that it was the path he was determined to follow.
Indiran had been in service for less than two years when he passed away. During that time, he had developed a reputation for his good attitude and humility.
He was also skilled in photography, often taking pictures at army camp events attended by senior officers, and had been trained to operate drones.
It is the everyday moments Usha misses most, particularly the calls Indiran would make to check on her.
“He would call several times a day and say, ‘Amma, how are you? Have you eaten? How’s your work today? Eat well, sleep well, take care'," she said.
“I really miss his calls, his voice. Nobody can replace him.”
About a week before his death, Usha had met Indiran in Taiping and cooked some of his favourite dishes, including fish sodhi, bayam and lala.
“We then went to a Chinese restaurant and I fed him, and he fed me,” Usha recalled. “He said, ‘Amma, luckily you came.’ It was the last dish I cooked for him, the food that he liked."
For Usha, the meaning of Deepavali has not changed; what is different is that her son is no longer there to share it with the family.
“Even though he’s not around, we feel that he’s here. We cannot see him, but all the family members can feel him,” she added.
“We are going to miss his funny attitude, silly jokes, and the love and laughter he brought into our lives.”
6719bbc13617e134: PETALING JAYA: Bagi Usha Suppiah, Deepavali sentiasa menjadi masa untuk berkumpul bersama keluarga. Rumahnya akan meriah dengan kehadiran saudara-mara, kesibukan menyediakan juadah perayaan dan anak-anak yang berkumpul untuk membuat muruku.
Namun, sambutan tahun ini berbeza kerana anak sulungnya, K Indiran, tiada lagi di sisi keluarga.
Pada 18 Feb lepas, anggota tentera berusia 22 tahun itu ditemukan tidak sedarkan diri di Kem Tentera Batu 10 di Kuantan. Dia menghembuskan nafas terakhir dua hari kemudian ketika menerima rawatan.
“Kali terakhir Indiran ada bersama kami, semuanya gembira. Tetapi tahun ini, dia sudah tiada. Apabila seorang ahli keluarga tiada, memang terasa ada sesuatu yang kurang.
“Saya sangat rindukannya. Semua ahli keluarga pun merinduinya. Tetapi kehidupan perlu diteruskan,” kata Usha, 52, kepada FMT Lifestyle.
Mengikut tradisi Hindu yang diamalkan keluarganya, mereka tidak akan meraikan Deepavali selama setahun selepas kematian ahli keluarga.
Bagaimanapun, Usha bersama tiga lagi anaknya tetap akan mengadakan upacara sembahyang dan pertemuan sederhana bersama saudara-mara yang datang dari seluruh negara.
Anak bongsunya yang berusia 12 tahun masih cuba memahami mengapa sambutan Deepavali tahun ini tidak lagi seperti dahulu.
“Dia bertanya, ‘Amma, kenapa Anna (abang) dah tak ada? Kita tak boleh sambut Deepavali, kan?’
“Saya beritahu dia, ‘Ya, Anna dah tak ada, tetapi kita tetap akan sembahyang. Kita tak sambut secara besar-besaran, cuma makan-makan bersama keluarga’,” kata Usha yang bekerja sebagai jururawat.

Pada tahun-tahun sebelumnya, Indiran akan pulang kira-kira seminggu sebelum Deepavali untuk membantu membersihkan dan menghias rumah, menemani ibunya membeli-belah serta menyediakan juadah tradisional seperti muruku.
Indiran juga sering menjadi penyeri setiap kali keluarga berkumpul, dengan telatahnya yang menghiburkan saudara-mara dan rakan-rakan.
“Pakcik dan kawan-kawan Indiran akan berkumpul dan minum bersama. Kemudian Indiran akan menari dan menyanyi.
“Kami semua seronok kerana dia akan menari bersama kami. Kenangan itu memang tak boleh saya lupakan,” kata Usha.
Selepas bapanya, seorang pegawai tentera udara, meninggal dunia dalam nahas pesawat pada 2016, Indiran mula memikul tanggungjawab lebih besar dalam keluarga.
Sebagai anak sulung daripada empat beradik, dia banyak membantu ibunya menguruskan rumah tangga dan menjaga adik-adiknya.
“Dia jaga adik-adiknya. Dia akan masak nasi, bersihkan rumah ... sama seperti suami saya, dia rajin bantu buat semua kerja rumah," kata Usha.
Susulan kehilangan suami dalam nahas pesawat, Usha pada mulanya keberatan membenarkan Indiran menyertai angkatan tentera.
Namun, beliau akhirnya akur dengan keputusan anaknya yang bertekad memilih kerjaya itu.

Indiran belum pun genap dua tahun berkhidmat dalam angkatan tentera ketika dia meninggal dunia. Sepanjang tempoh perkhidmatannya, Indiran dikenali sebagai seorang yang mempunyai keperibadian yang baik dan merendah diri.
Dia juga mahir dalam bidang fotografi dan sering mengambil gambar pada acara di kem tentera yang dihadiri pegawai kanan, selain pernah menerima latihan mengendalikan dron.
Namun, perkara yang paling dirindui Usha ialah kenangan kecil dalam kehidupan seharian bersama anaknya, terutama panggilan telefon Indiran yang sentiasa bertanyakan khabarnya.
“Dia akan telefon beberapa kali sehari dan tanya, ‘Amma, apa khabar? Dah makan? Macam mana kerja hari ini? Makan elok-elok, tidur cukup-cukup, jaga diri.’
“Saya sangat rindukan panggilan dan suaranya. Tiada siapa boleh menggantikan tempatnya," kata Usha.
Kira-kira seminggu sebelum kematian Indiran, Usha sempat bertemu anaknya di Taiping dan memasak beberapa hidangan kegemarannya, termasuk sodhi ikan, bayam dan lala.
“Kemudian kami pergi ke sebuah restoran Cina. Saya suapkan dia makanan dan dia pun suapkan saya.
“Dia kata, ‘Amma, nasib baik Amma datang.’ Itulah kali terakhir saya masak makanan kegemarannya,” katanya.

“Walaupun dia sudah tiada, kami masih rasa seolah-olah dia ada bersama kami. Kami tak dapat lihatnya, tetapi seluruh keluarga masih dapat rasakan kehadirannya.

47951b9efc629918: Nvidia’s board has opened an investigation into its CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to an affair, amid allegations he had a commercial relationship with a woman US authorities feel is likely a Chinese spy.

The AI hardware giant’s board published a statement on Sunday afternoon that states it is “initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”

The New York Times is the source of that reporting. On October 29 it alleged US government intelligence agencies decided to investigate a woman who goes by Alice Huang and/or Huang Le, on grounds she passes intelligence with Beijing.
In that story The Times used the term “close relationship” to describe the Nvidia CEO's associations with both Ms Huang and US president Donald Trump.
On Sunday the newspaper alleged US authorities believe Alice Huang and Jensen Huang shared a "romantic" relationship.

The Times further alleges Ms Huang is a Chinese citizen who worked for a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed that has bought plenty of Nvidia hardware and is suspected of doing so to make it available to Chinese users, either by running inside datacenters or facilitating transport to the Middle Kingdom.

The US has for years banned or restricted exports of advanced GPUs to China, partly because it feels Beijing’s armed forces can use them to build systems that will erode America’s military superiority.

Any relationship, of any sort, between Jensen Huang and a Chinese intelligence operative would therefore be enormously concerning. The company told The Times that Jensen Huang and Alice Huang just had normal CEO-to-customer-exec chats that were no threat to Nvidia intellectual property or US national security.
Shortly after Nvidia’s board published its statement, Huang sent an email to staff that the company made public.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” the email opens. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Huang’s email doesn’t explicitly link his actions to The Times’ reports, but he says he supports the Nvidia board’s decision to open its investigation “and will cooperate fully.”
“I love our country and our company,” Huang wrote. “I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.”
The CEO’s mail, and the Board’s statement, make no allegations about any “close relationship” with Ms. Huang.

The exact nature of that relationship therefore remains mysterious, as does Nvidia’s relationship with Singapore, a tiny island nation that has sometimes been the source of 22 percent of the company’s revenue.

Singapore is simply incapable of hosting as much Nvidia kit as that volume of purchases would buy, because its government limits datacenters to 1.6 GW of energy consumption. When asked to explain that oddity, Nvidia has said that it’s satisfied Singaporean entities buy its hardware on behalf of end-users in other locations, and that such deals are not used to evade the USA’s sanctions.

Nvidia is not a notably scandal-prone company, but in 2022 it did admit to having previously misrepresented the impact of cryptocurrency mining on sales of its gaming hardware. China has opened an antitrust case, and US authorities may have considered doing likewise.

Jensen Huang, however, has never presented as the kind of CEO who makes operating at the edge of the law a regular tactic. Nor does he hold sufficient Nvidia shares or voting power to unilaterally make major decisions.
This leaves the leader of the world’s top AI company appearing to have made a very human error. ®
